concepts.name: Periodic table arrangement and periodic trends
concepts.explanation: The periodic table as an arrangement of elements that reveals trends in physical and chemical properties.

concepts.name: Element symbols (elements 1–36)
concepts.explanation: Recognition and correct use of chemical symbols for the first 36 elements.

concepts.name: Main-group similarities (alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens, noble gases)
concepts.explanation: Principal resemblances in properties among elements within key main groups: alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens, and noble gases.

concepts.name: Ordering elements by relative atomic mass (historical approach)
concepts.explanation: Arranging elements in order of relative atomic mass and noting differences compared with the modern periodic table.

concepts.name: Reactivity of Group 1 metals with water (Li, Na, K)
concepts.explanation: Demonstration and comparison of how lithium, sodium, and potassium react with water as an illustration of group trends.

concepts.name: Particle model of matter (atoms, molecules, ions)
concepts.explanation: Matter is composed of particles, which may be atoms, molecules, or ions.

concepts.name: Atoms are extremely small (minute size of atoms)
concepts.explanation: Atoms are minute; understanding that atomic dimensions are far smaller than can be observed directly.

concepts.name: Law of conservation of mass
concepts.explanation: In a chemical reaction, mass is conserved (total mass of reactants equals total mass of products).

concepts.name: Subatomic particles: charge, relative mass, and location
concepts.explanation: Key properties of electrons, protons, and neutrons including relative charge, relative mass, and where each is found in the atom.

concepts.name: Atomic number (Z)
concepts.explanation: Atomic number (Z) as the number of protons in the nucleus (and equals the number of electrons in a neutral atom).

concepts.name: Mass number (A)
concepts.explanation: Mass number (A) as the total number of protons plus neutrons in the nucleus.

concepts.name: Isotopes (hydrogen and carbon examples)
concepts.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element (same Z) with different mass numbers; illustrated using hydrogen and carbon isotopes.

concepts.name: Relative atomic mass (Ar)
concepts.explanation: Relative atomic mass (Ar) as the weighted average mass of an element’s atoms relative to a standard scale.

concepts.name: Carbon-12 scale for relative atomic masses
concepts.explanation: Definition of the relative atomic mass scale based on assigning carbon-12 an exact mass of 12 units.

concepts.name: Dalton’s atomic theory (outline)
concepts.explanation: Core principles of Dalton’s atomic theory as an early model explaining matter and chemical change.

concepts.name: Thomson’s discovery of the electron (negative charge)
concepts.explanation: Thomson’s contribution: identification of the electron and its negative charge as a component of atoms.

concepts.name: Rutherford’s alpha-particle scattering experiment
concepts.explanation: The alpha-particle scattering experiment and how it supports the existence of a small, dense nucleus.

concepts.name: Bohr model of the atom (outline)
concepts.explanation: Bohr’s model as a refinement of atomic structure (electrons in energy levels) at an outline level.

concepts.name: Mass spectrometer use in determining relative atomic mass
concepts.explanation: Using mass spectrometry data (isotopic masses and abundances) to determine an element’s relative atomic mass.

concepts.name: Mendeleev’s periodic table and comparison with the modern table
concepts.explanation: Key features of Mendeleev’s periodic table and how it differs from the modern periodic table.

concepts.name: Moseley’s contribution to the periodic table (atomic number basis)
concepts.explanation: Moseley’s role in establishing atomic number as the correct basis for ordering elements in the periodic table.

concepts.name: Electronic energy levels in atoms
concepts.explanation: Electrons in atoms occupy discrete main energy levels (shells) with increasing energy further from the nucleus.

concepts.name: Electron arrangement for elements 1–20
concepts.explanation: Determining the number of electrons in each main energy level for atoms of the first 20 elements.

concepts.name: Valence (outer) electrons and periodic classification (first 20 elements)
concepts.explanation: Classifying the first 20 elements based on the number of outer-shell electrons, linking this to periodic table position.

concepts.name: Covalent (atomic) radius
concepts.explanation: Defining atomic radius using covalent radii (half the distance between nuclei in a covalent bond) for main-group elements.

concepts.name: Trend in covalent radius down a group
concepts.explanation: Explaining why covalent radii generally increase down a group due to additional energy levels and increased shielding.

concepts.name: Trend in covalent radius across a period (main-group)
concepts.explanation: Explaining why covalent radii generally decrease across a period due to increasing nuclear charge with similar shielding.

concepts.name: Dependence of chemical properties on electronic structure
concepts.explanation: Connecting an element’s reactivity and typical compounds to its outer-electron configuration.

concepts.name: Screening (shielding) effect
concepts.explanation: Inner electrons reduce the effective nuclear attraction experienced by outer electrons, influencing atomic size and reactivity trends.

concepts.name: Nuclear charge and periodic trends (Groups I and VII)
concepts.explanation: Using nuclear charge (and effective nuclear charge) to explain trends in properties such as reactivity in Groups 1 and 7.

concepts.name: Alpha radiation (nature and penetrating ability)
concepts.explanation: Identifying alpha radiation as helium nuclei and describing its low penetrating power.

concepts.name: Beta radiation (nature and penetrating ability)
concepts.explanation: Identifying beta radiation as fast electrons and describing its moderate penetrating power.

concepts.name: Gamma radiation (nature and penetrating ability)
concepts.explanation: Identifying gamma radiation as high-energy electromagnetic radiation and describing its high penetrating power.

concepts.name: Radioisotopes
concepts.explanation: Atoms of the same element with unstable nuclei that emit radiation as they decay.

concepts.name: Half-life (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: The time taken for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay, treated conceptually without calculations.

concepts.name: Detection and penetrating power of radiation (demonstration)
concepts.explanation: Demonstrating that radiation can be detected and that alpha, beta, and gamma differ in penetrating ability using shielding comparisons.

concepts.name: Radiocarbon (14C) age determination (concept)
concepts.explanation: Using the decay of carbon-14 in once-living materials to estimate age without requiring calculations.

concepts.name: Oxidation as loss of electrons
concepts.explanation: Defining oxidation in terms of electron loss in simple redox reactions.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Reduction as gain of electrons
concepts.explanation: Defining reduction in terms of electron gain in simple redox reactions.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Oxidising agent
concepts.explanation: A substance that causes oxidation by accepting electrons (it is reduced).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Reducing agent
concepts.explanation: A substance that causes reduction by donating electrons (it is oxidised).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrochemical series (reactivity series) as ease of oxidation
concepts.explanation: Arranging metals by their tendency to be oxidised (lose electrons), used to predict which metals react more readily.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolysis of copper(II) sulfate using copper electrodes
concepts.explanation: Describing electrolysis where copper dissolves at the anode and copper is deposited at the cathode in CuSO4(aq).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolysis of acidified water using inert electrodes
concepts.explanation: Describing electrolysis producing hydrogen at the cathode and oxygen at the anode with inert electrodes.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Half-equations for redox processes
concepts.explanation: Representing oxidation and reduction separately with electron transfer using half-equations.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Ionic movement in electrolysis
concepts.explanation: Cations migrate to the cathode and anions migrate to the anode during electrolysis.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Flame tests for metal ions (Li, Na, K, Ba, Sr, Cu)
concepts.explanation: Using characteristic flame colours to identify specific metal ions in salts.

concepts.name: Halogens as oxidising agents (Group VII redox reactions)
concepts.explanation: Using displacement/redox reactions to show halogens oxidise halide ions and other reducing agents (e.g., Fe2+, sulfite).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Metal displacement reactions (e.g., Zn with Cu2+, Mg with Cu2+)
concepts.explanation: More reactive metals displace less reactive metal ions from solution via electron transfer.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Chemical compounds
concepts.explanation: A compound is a pure substance made of two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions.

concepts.name: Simple chemical formulas
concepts.explanation: Writing formulas to show the types and numbers of atoms/ions in a substance using standard symbols and subscripts.

concepts.name: Noble gas electron configuration stability
concepts.explanation: Noble gases have stable outer electron arrangements, helping explain low reactivity and driving forces for bonding in other elements.

concepts.name: Valency as achieving stable electronic structure
concepts.explanation: Valency relates to how atoms combine (lose, gain, or share electrons) to attain a more stable outer electron arrangement.

concepts.name: Octet rule
concepts.explanation: Many atoms tend to form bonds to achieve eight electrons in their outer shell (noble gas configuration), especially in main-group elements.

concepts.name: Limitations of the octet rule
concepts.explanation: Recognising that the octet rule does not apply universally and is an approximate model rather than a strict rule.

concepts.name: Predicting formulas of binary compounds using the octet rule (first 36 elements excluding d-block)
concepts.explanation: Using typical valencies/ion charges inferred from electron configurations to write formulas of simple binary compounds for main-group elements.

concepts.name: Predicting formulas of hydroxides and carbonates (main-group, where they exist)
concepts.explanation: Writing correct compound formulas involving OH− and CO3^2− by balancing ionic charges with main-group cations.

concepts.name: Positive and negative ions
concepts.explanation: Cations form by electron loss and anions form by electron gain, producing charged particles involved in ionic bonding.

concepts.name: Ionic bonding as electron transfer
concepts.explanation: An ionic bond forms when electrons transfer from one atom to another, creating oppositely charged ions held by electrostatic attraction.

concepts.name: Dot-and-cross diagrams for ionic bonding
concepts.explanation: Representing electron transfer and resulting ions using dot-and-cross notation to track electron origins.

concepts.name: Sodium chloride crystal structure
concepts.explanation: Describing NaCl as a giant ionic lattice of alternating Na+ and Cl− ions arranged in a regular 3D structure.

concepts.name: Characteristics of ionic substances
concepts.explanation: Typical properties of ionic compounds (e.g., high melting points, conductivity when molten/aqueous, brittle crystals) linked to ionic lattices.

concepts.name: Covalent bonding (sharing electron pairs)
concepts.explanation: A chemical bond formed when atoms share one or more pairs of electrons to achieve stable electron configurations.

concepts.name: Single covalent bond
concepts.explanation: A covalent bond consisting of one shared pair of electrons between two atoms.

concepts.name: Double covalent bond
concepts.explanation: A covalent bond consisting of two shared pairs of electrons between two atoms.

concepts.name: Triple covalent bond
concepts.explanation: A covalent bond consisting of three shared pairs of electrons between two atoms.

concepts.name: Polar covalent bond
concepts.explanation: A covalent bond where electrons are shared unequally due to a difference in electronegativity, creating partial charges (δ+ and δ−).

concepts.name: Non-polar covalent bond
concepts.explanation: A covalent bond where electrons are shared equally or nearly equally, resulting in no significant separation of charge.

concepts.name: Dot-and-cross diagram (covalent bonding)
concepts.explanation: A representation of covalent bonding showing valence electrons from different atoms (dots and crosses) and shared electron pairs in a bond.

concepts.name: Characteristics of covalent substances
concepts.explanation: Typical physical properties of covalent substances (e.g., lower melting/boiling points, poor electrical conductivity) linked to bonding and structure.

concepts.name: Polarity test for liquids using a charged plastic rod
concepts.explanation: An experiment to distinguish polar and non-polar liquids by observing whether a thin stream of liquid is deflected by a charged rod.

concepts.name: Solubility testing of ionic vs covalent substances in different solvents
concepts.explanation: A practical procedure comparing how ionic and covalent substances dissolve in polar and non-polar solvents to infer bonding type and intermolecular interactions.

concepts.name: Molecules as discrete particles
concepts.explanation: A molecule is a group of atoms covalently bonded together and acting as a single particle in many contexts.

concepts.name: Examples of materials in everyday life
concepts.explanation: Identifying and classifying common materials encountered in daily life by giving examples for different material categories.

concepts.name: Electronegativity
concepts.explanation: A measure of an atom’s attraction for shared (bonding) electrons in a chemical bond.

concepts.name: Periodic trend of electronegativity down a group
concepts.explanation: Electronegativity generally decreases down a group due to increased atomic radius and shielding reducing attraction for bonding electrons.

concepts.name: Periodic trend of electronegativity across a period
concepts.explanation: Electronegativity generally increases across a period due to increasing effective nuclear charge and decreasing atomic radius.

concepts.name: Bond polarity from electronegativity difference
concepts.explanation: Differences in electronegativity between bonded atoms create unequal electron sharing, producing partial charges and a polar bond.

concepts.name: Predicting bond type using electronegativity difference
concepts.explanation: Using electronegativity differences to classify bonds (e.g., nonpolar covalent, polar covalent, ionic) based on degree of electron sharing/transfer.

concepts.name: Molecular shapes of simple molecules (model-based)
concepts.explanation: Using physical models (e.g., balloons) to represent and identify the 3D shapes of simple molecules.

concepts.name: Test for chloride ions in aqueous solution
concepts.explanation: Qualitative analysis procedure to detect Cl− in solution using characteristic reagent reactions and observations (precipitate formation).

concepts.name: Test for carbonate ions in aqueous solution
concepts.explanation: Qualitative analysis procedure to detect CO3^2− in solution based on characteristic reaction observations (e.g., gas evolution).

concepts.name: Test for nitrate ions in aqueous solution
concepts.explanation: Qualitative analysis procedure to detect NO3− in solution using characteristic reagent reactions and observations.

concepts.name: Test for sulfate ions in aqueous solution
concepts.explanation: Qualitative analysis procedure to detect SO4^2− in solution using characteristic reagent reactions and observations (precipitate formation).

concepts.name: Avogadro constant
concepts.explanation: The number of specified particles (atoms, molecules, ions, etc.) in one mole (approximately 6.02 × 10^23 mol⁻1).

concepts.name: Mole (amount of substance)
concepts.explanation: The SI unit for amount of substance; one mole contains Avogadro’s number of particles.

concepts.name: Standard temperature and pressure (s.t.p.)
concepts.explanation: Reference conditions used for gases; used to compare gas volumes and to correct measured gas volumes to standard conditions.

concepts.name: Molar volume of a gas at s.t.p.
concepts.explanation: The volume occupied by one mole of an ideal gas at s.t.p.; used to convert between moles and gas volume at standard conditions.

concepts.name: Molar mass
concepts.explanation: The mass of one mole of a substance (g mol⁻1), used to convert between mass and moles.

concepts.name: Relative molecular mass (Mr)
concepts.explanation: The sum of relative atomic masses of atoms in a molecule; dimensionless quantity used in formula/mole calculations.

concepts.name: Calculation of Mr from relative atomic masses
concepts.explanation: Procedure for finding relative molecular mass by adding the relative atomic masses of each atom in the molecular formula with correct subscripts.

concepts.name: Moles to mass conversion
concepts.explanation: Converting amount in moles to mass in grams using mass = moles × molar mass.

concepts.name: Mass to moles conversion
concepts.explanation: Converting mass in grams to moles using moles = mass ÷ molar mass.

concepts.name: Moles to number of particles conversion
concepts.explanation: Converting moles to number of particles using particles = moles × Avogadro constant.

concepts.name: Number of particles to moles conversion
concepts.explanation: Converting number of particles to moles using moles = particles ÷ Avogadro constant.

concepts.name: Gas volume to moles conversion at s.t.p.
concepts.explanation: Converting a gas volume at s.t.p. to moles using molar volume at s.t.p.

concepts.name: Moles to gas volume conversion at s.t.p.
concepts.explanation: Converting moles of a gas to volume at s.t.p. using molar volume at s.t.p.

concepts.name: Boyle's law
concepts.explanation: For a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, pressure is inversely proportional to volume (P ∝ 1/V).

concepts.name: Charles's law
concepts.explanation: For a fixed mass of gas at constant pressure, volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature (V ∝ T).

concepts.name: Combined gas law
concepts.explanation: For a fixed mass of gas, relates pressure, volume and temperature: P1V1/T1 = P2V2/T2.

concepts.name: Correction of gas volumes to s.t.p.
concepts.explanation: Using gas-law relationships to convert a measured gas volume at given P and T to the equivalent volume at s.t.p. (using Pa, cm^3, K).

concepts.name: Diffusion
concepts.explanation: The net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration due to random motion, observed in gases and liquids.

concepts.name: Particle motion in solids, liquids and gases
concepts.explanation: Model describing differences in particle arrangement and movement across the three states of matter.

concepts.name: Empirical formula
concepts.explanation: The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of each element in a compound.

concepts.name: Molecular formula
concepts.explanation: Shows the actual number of atoms of each element in a molecule; can be a multiple of the empirical formula.

concepts.name: Percentage composition by mass
concepts.explanation: The mass percentage of each element in a compound, calculated from formula masses or used to determine empirical formula.

concepts.name: Structural formula
concepts.explanation: A representation showing how atoms are arranged and connected (bonding pattern) in a molecule.

concepts.name: Empirical formula calculation from percent composition
concepts.explanation: Procedure: convert percent masses to moles for each element, divide by the smallest, and scale to whole numbers to obtain the empirical formula.

concepts.name: Molecular formula calculation from empirical formula and Mr
concepts.explanation: Determine the multiplier n = Mr/(empirical formula mass) and multiply subscripts in the empirical formula by n to get the molecular formula.

concepts.name: Chemical equation
concepts.explanation: Symbolic representation of a chemical reaction showing reactants, products, and stoichiometric coefficients.

concepts.name: Balancing chemical equations
concepts.explanation: Adjusting coefficients in a chemical equation to satisfy conservation of atoms for each element.

concepts.name: Stoichiometric calculations from balanced equations using the mole concept
concepts.explanation: Using mole ratios from balanced equations (given) to calculate reacting masses and product yields, including conversions involving masses and gas volumes.

concepts.name: Mandatory experiment: Determination of the relative molecular mass of a volatile liquid
concepts.explanation: Experimental determination of Mr of a volatile liquid using a conical flask or gas syringe by relating measured mass and gas volume under known conditions.

concepts.name: Solution concentration (molarity, mol L−1)
concepts.explanation: Definition and use of molarity as moles of solute per litre of solution (mol L−1).

concepts.name: Primary standard
concepts.explanation: A highly pure, stable substance of known formula mass used to prepare solutions of accurately known concentration.

concepts.name: Standard solution
concepts.explanation: A solution with accurately known concentration, prepared from a primary standard or by standardisation.

concepts.name: Calculation of molarity from g L−1 (and vice versa)
concepts.explanation: Convert between concentration in grams per litre and molarity using molar mass (c(mol L−1)=c(g L−1)/M).

concepts.name: Moles from molarity and volume
concepts.explanation: Use n = c × V (with V in litres) to calculate amount of substance from solution concentration and volume.

concepts.name: Percentage concentration (% v/v)
concepts.explanation: Express concentration as volume of solute per 100 mL of solution (% v/v), commonly for liquid mixtures.

concepts.name: Colour intensity as an indicator of concentration (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: Simple relationship that more concentrated coloured solutions generally appear more intensely coloured (qualitative treatment).

concepts.name: Acid
concepts.explanation: Substance that shows acidic properties; in Arrhenius terms (aqueous) produces H+ (or H3O+) ions in water.

concepts.name: Base
concepts.explanation: Substance that shows basic properties; in Arrhenius terms (aqueous) produces OH− ions in water.

concepts.name: Salt
concepts.explanation: Ionic compound formed when the hydrogen ion(s) of an acid are replaced by metal or ammonium ions, often produced by neutralisation.

concepts.name: Neutralisation reaction
concepts.explanation: Reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt (and typically water), forming the basis of acid–base titrations.

concepts.name: Arrhenius theory of acids and bases (aqueous only)
concepts.explanation: Model defining acids as producers of H+ (H3O+) in water and bases as producers of OH− in water; limited to aqueous solutions.

concepts.name: Volumetric analysis apparatus
concepts.explanation: Identification and correct use of key titration apparatus (e.g., burette, pipette, volumetric flask, conical flask) in quantitative analysis.

concepts.name: Correct titrimetric procedure
concepts.explanation: Stepwise technique for performing accurate titrations (rinsing, filling burette, pipetting aliquot, adding indicator, titrating to endpoint, repeat for concordant titres).

concepts.name: Acid-base titration
concepts.explanation: Use of titration to determine concentration by reacting measured volumes of acid and base to an endpoint/equivalence condition.

concepts.name: Volumetric problem solving (formula method)
concepts.explanation: Solve titration/concentration problems using balanced equations and stoichiometric relationships among moles, concentration, and volume.

concepts.name: Preparation of a standard solution of sodium carbonate (Na2CO3)
concepts.explanation: Mandatory practical: accurately weigh sodium carbonate, dissolve, and make up to volume in a volumetric flask to produce a standard solution.

concepts.name: Standardisation of hydrochloric acid using sodium carbonate
concepts.explanation: Mandatory practical: determine the exact concentration of HCl by titrating it against a standard Na2CO3 solution using stoichiometry.

concepts.name: Hydrochloric acid–sodium hydroxide titration
concepts.explanation: Mandatory practical: titration of HCl with NaOH (strong acid–strong base) to determine concentration or perform quantitative neutralisation.

concepts.name: Preparation of sodium chloride by titration
concepts.explanation: Use measured neutralisation of HCl and NaOH (from titration data) followed by evaporation to obtain NaCl as a product salt.

concepts.name: Exothermic reaction
concepts.explanation: A chemical or physical change that releases heat to the surroundings, causing a temperature rise; associated with negative enthalpy change (ΔH < 0).

concepts.name: Endothermic reaction
concepts.explanation: A chemical or physical change that absorbs heat from the surroundings, causing a temperature drop; associated with positive enthalpy change (ΔH > 0).

concepts.name: Enthalpy change (ΔH) sign convention
concepts.explanation: The rule that ΔH is negative for exothermic processes and positive for endothermic processes when measured at constant pressure.

concepts.name: Heat of reaction
concepts.explanation: The heat energy change accompanying a chemical reaction, usually expressed as an enthalpy change (ΔH) per mole of reaction as written.

concepts.name: Combustion of hydrocarbons
concepts.explanation: Exothermic reaction of a hydrocarbon with oxygen producing carbon dioxide and water (complete combustion) and releasing heat.

concepts.name: Heat of combustion
concepts.explanation: The enthalpy change when one mole of a substance is completely burned in oxygen under specified conditions.

concepts.name: Bomb calorimeter
concepts.explanation: A calorimetry apparatus that measures heats of combustion accurately by burning a sample in oxygen in a sealed, constant-volume metal vessel surrounded by water.

concepts.name: Calorific value (kJ kg⁻¹) of a fuel
concepts.explanation: Energy released per kilogram of fuel on complete combustion; used to compare fuels for heating and energy applications.

concepts.name: Heat of neutralisation experiment (HCl + NaOH)
concepts.explanation: Calorimetric determination of the heat change when hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide; a standard experiment to measure heat of reaction.

concepts.name: Hydrocarbon sources: fossil fuels
concepts.explanation: Coal, petroleum (crude oil) and natural gas as major natural sources of hydrocarbons used as fuels and chemical feedstocks.

concepts.name: Methane production by decomposition (biogas)
concepts.explanation: Generation of methane from anaerobic decomposition of animal waste and vegetation.

concepts.name: Methane hazards in confined environments
concepts.explanation: Safety risks from methane accumulation (flammability/explosion risk) in slurry pits, coal mines and refuse dumps.

concepts.name: Methane as a greenhouse gas
concepts.explanation: Methane contributes to the greenhouse effect due to its infrared absorption and role in atmospheric warming.

concepts.name: Homologous series (alkanes, alkenes, alkynes)
concepts.explanation: Families of organic compounds with the same functional group and general formula, showing gradation in properties with increasing chain length.

concepts.name: Systematic naming of alkanes (to C5)
concepts.explanation: IUPAC-based naming of straight-chain and branched alkanes up to five carbons.

concepts.name: Structural formula representation of hydrocarbons
concepts.explanation: Use of displayed/structural formulas to show atom connectivity in alkanes, alkenes and alkynes.

concepts.name: Structural isomerism in alkanes (to C5)
concepts.explanation: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different connectivity of atoms, illustrated using alkanes up to five carbons.

concepts.name: Systematic naming of alkenes (to C4)
concepts.explanation: IUPAC-based naming of alkenes up to four carbons, including position of the double bond.

concepts.name: Structural isomerism in alkenes (to C4)
concepts.explanation: Isomerism among alkenes up to four carbons due to different carbon skeletons or different double-bond positions (structural only).

concepts.name: Cyclohexane structure (cycloalkane)
concepts.explanation: A cyclic saturated hydrocarbon structure used as an example of a ring alkane.

concepts.name: Iso-octane (2,2,4-trimethylpentane) structure
concepts.explanation: Branched C8 alkane structure used as a reference compound in petrol octane rating contexts.

concepts.name: Qualitative solubility of hydrocarbons
concepts.explanation: Hydrocarbons are generally insoluble in water and soluble in non-polar solvents; demonstrated for methane, ethene and ethyne (qualitative only).

concepts.name: Aromatic compounds: benzene ring structure
concepts.explanation: Benzene as an aromatic hydrocarbon with a ring structure and delocalised bonding (structural awareness at this level).

concepts.name: Methylbenzene (toluene) structure
concepts.explanation: An aromatic hydrocarbon consisting of a benzene ring with a methyl substituent; used as an example aromatic compound.

concepts.name: Ethylbenzene structure
concepts.explanation: An aromatic hydrocarbon consisting of a benzene ring with an ethyl substituent; used as an example aromatic compound.

concepts.name: Fractional distillation (fractionation) of crude oil
concepts.explanation: Separation of crude oil into fractions based on boiling point differences using a fractionating column.

concepts.name: Major crude oil fractions and typical uses
concepts.explanation: Identification of refinery gas, light gasoline, naphtha, kerosene, gas oil and residue fractions and their common applications.

concepts.name: Natural gas composition
concepts.explanation: Natural gas as a gaseous fuel mixture mainly of methane with smaller amounts of other hydrocarbons/impurities.

concepts.name: Liquid petroleum gas (LPG) composition
concepts.explanation: LPG as a fuel mixture primarily of propane and butane stored under pressure as a liquid.

concepts.name: Odorisation of natural gas with mercaptans
concepts.explanation: Addition of strongly smelling mercaptans to otherwise odourless natural gas to aid leak detection and improve safety.

concepts.name: Petrol composition as a hydrocarbon blend
concepts.explanation: Petrol (gasoline) as a mixture of hydrocarbons formulated to meet performance requirements in engines.

concepts.name: Auto-ignition and engine knocking
concepts.explanation: Premature ignition of fuel-air mixtures in engines causing knocking; related to fuel composition and resistance to auto-ignition.

concepts.name: Octane number
concepts.explanation: A measure of a fuel's resistance to knocking (tendency to auto-ignite) in spark-ignition engines.

concepts.name: Lead additives in petrol
concepts.explanation: Use of lead compounds historically added to petrol to improve octane rating and reduce knocking, with associated concerns.

concepts.name: Isomerisation to improve octane rating
concepts.explanation: Refinery process converting straight-chain alkanes into branched isomers to increase octane number.
concepts.broader_concept: Refinery processes to improve fuel quality

concepts.name: Dehydrocyclisation to improve octane rating
concepts.explanation: Refinery process converting alkanes to cyclic/aromatic compounds (with hydrogen removal) to increase octane number.
concepts.broader_concept: Refinery processes to improve fuel quality

concepts.name: Catalytic cracking
concepts.explanation: Industrial process breaking long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter alkanes and alkenes using a catalyst to increase petrol yield and improve fuel quality.

concepts.name: Ethyne (acetylene) preparation
concepts.explanation: Laboratory preparation of ethyne as a chemical fuel (specific reagents not detailed in the provided text).

concepts.name: Tests for unsaturation using bromine water
concepts.explanation: Detection of carbon–carbon multiple bonds by decolourisation of bromine water under suitable conditions.

concepts.name: Tests for unsaturation using acidified potassium manganate(VII)
concepts.explanation: Detection of carbon–carbon multiple bonds using acidified KMnO4, typically observed by loss of purple colour (and/or formation of products) as it oxidises unsaturated compounds.

concepts.name: Oxyacetylene welding and cutting
concepts.explanation: Use of ethyne combusted in oxygen to produce a high-temperature flame for welding and cutting metals.

concepts.name: Hydrogen production by electrolysis of water
concepts.explanation: Manufacture of hydrogen gas by passing electric current through water (with appropriate electrolyte) to decompose it into hydrogen and oxygen.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Hydrogen production by steam reforming of natural gas
concepts.explanation: Industrial manufacture of hydrogen from natural gas by reaction with steam (simple treatment).

concepts.name: Factors affecting rate of reaction
concepts.explanation: Key variables that change reaction rate: concentration, particle size (surface area), temperature, nature of reactants, and catalysts.

concepts.name: Effect of concentration on reaction rate
concepts.explanation: Higher reactant concentration generally increases collision frequency, increasing reaction rate.

concepts.name: Effect of temperature on reaction rate
concepts.explanation: Increasing temperature generally increases reaction rate by raising particle kinetic energy and the fraction of collisions with sufficient energy.

concepts.name: Effect of particle size (surface area) on reaction rate
concepts.explanation: Smaller particle size increases surface area available for collisions, typically increasing reaction rate for solids.

concepts.name: Nature of reactants and reaction rate
concepts.explanation: Different reactants (bond types, phase, structure) react at different rates under the same conditions.

concepts.name: Catalyst
concepts.explanation: A substance that increases reaction rate without being consumed overall, typically by providing an alternative pathway.

concepts.name: Catalyst poison
concepts.explanation: A substance that reduces or stops catalytic activity (often by binding to active sites).

concepts.name: Enzymes as catalysts
concepts.explanation: Biological catalysts produced by living cells that speed up specific reactions under mild conditions.

concepts.name: Dust explosion
concepts.explanation: Rapid combustion of fine particulate solids in air due to very high surface area and rapid reaction rate.
concepts.broader_concept: Effect of surface area on reaction rate

concepts.name: Monitoring rate of oxygen production from hydrogen peroxide (MnO2 catalyst)
concepts.explanation: Mandatory practical: measure reaction rate by tracking O2 produced during H2O2 decomposition using manganese dioxide as a catalyst.

concepts.name: Sodium thiosulfate and hydrochloric acid rate experiment (effects of concentration and temperature)
concepts.explanation: Mandatory practical: investigate how changing concentration and temperature affects the rate of reaction between sodium thiosulfate solution and hydrochloric acid (often monitored by loss of visibility due to sulfur formation).

concepts.name: Catalytic oxidation of methanol using hot platinum or nichrome
concepts.explanation: Demonstration: oxidation of methanol accelerated by a heated metal catalyst (platinum or nichrome) illustrating catalytic action.

concepts.name: Catalysed oxidation of potassium sodium tartrate by hydrogen peroxide (Co(II) salts)
concepts.explanation: Demonstration: hydrogen peroxide oxidizes potassium sodium tartrate more rapidly in the presence of cobalt(II) salts as a catalyst.

concepts.name: Catalytic converter
concepts.explanation: Vehicle exhaust device using catalysts to convert harmful gases into less harmful products.

concepts.name: Catalysts used in catalytic converters
concepts.explanation: The catalyst materials (commonly noble metals) and their role as heterogeneous catalysts in exhaust treatment.

concepts.name: Reactions catalysed in a catalytic converter
concepts.explanation: Key exhaust-cleaning reactions promoted by the converter (e.g., oxidation of CO and hydrocarbons; reduction of nitrogen oxides).

concepts.name: Environmental benefits of catalytic converters
concepts.explanation: Reduction of air pollutants (e.g., carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, unburned hydrocarbons) through catalytic conversion in vehicle exhaust systems.

concepts.name: Rate of reaction
concepts.explanation: The speed of a chemical reaction, expressed as the change in concentration of a reactant consumed or product formed per unit time.

concepts.name: Saturated organic compounds
concepts.explanation: Organic compounds containing only single carbon–carbon bonds (no C=C or C≡C), characteristic of alkanes and many alcohols.
concepts.broader_concept: Classification of organic compounds by bonding

concepts.name: Unsaturated organic compounds
concepts.explanation: Organic compounds containing at least one multiple bond (typically C=C), leading to characteristic addition reactions.
concepts.broader_concept: Classification of organic compounds by bonding

concepts.name: Tetrahedral carbon (sp3) structure
concepts.explanation: Carbon bonded to four atoms by single bonds has a tetrahedral arrangement (approx. 109.5°), typical of alkanes and alcohol carbons.

concepts.name: Planar carbon at a double bond (sp2) structure
concepts.explanation: Carbon atoms involved in a C=C or C=O double bond are approximately trigonal planar (~120°) around the double-bonded carbon.

concepts.name: Alkane homologous series (up to C4)
concepts.explanation: Structures and names of the first four alkanes (methane to butane) and recognition of the alkane functional class.

concepts.name: Alkene homologous series (up to C4)
concepts.explanation: Structures and names of the first four carbon alkenes and recognition of the C=C functional group.

concepts.name: Non-polar character of the C=C bond in alkenes (syllabus treatment)
concepts.explanation: At this level, the alkene double bond is treated as non-polar, influencing solubility trends and reactivity patterns taught (e.g., addition).
concepts.broader_concept: Polarity and properties of organic functional groups

concepts.name: Alcohol functional group and classification (primary vs secondary)
concepts.explanation: Recognition of the -OH group and classification of alcohols as primary or secondary based on the carbon bearing the -OH group.

concepts.name: Alcohol nomenclature (up to C4)
concepts.explanation: IUPAC naming of alcohols up to four carbons (including position of -OH), restricted to primary and secondary alcohols.

concepts.name: Carbonyl compounds: aldehyde functional group (up to C4)
concepts.explanation: Recognition of aldehydes (terminal -CHO) and structure/nomenclature of aldehydes up to four carbons.

concepts.name: Polarity of the C=O bond in aldehydes
concepts.explanation: The carbonyl (C=O) bond is polar, affecting physical properties such as solubility and typical reactivity (e.g., oxidation).
concepts.broader_concept: Polarity and properties of organic functional groups

concepts.name: Carboxylic acid functional group and nomenclature (up to C4)
concepts.explanation: Recognition of -COOH and structure/naming of carboxylic acids up to four carbons (e.g., methanoic, ethanoic acids).
concepts.broader_concept: Carboxylic acids: structure, naming, and properties

concepts.name: Polarity associated with the carboxyl group (C=O in acids)
concepts.explanation: Carboxylic acids contain a polar carbonyl bond, contributing to characteristic solubility/physical property trends emphasized in the syllabus.
concepts.broader_concept: Polarity and properties of organic functional groups

concepts.name: Qualitative solubility of organic compounds in water vs non-polar solvents
concepts.explanation: Using polarity to predict/compare whether organic substances dissolve better in water or in non-polar solvents (qualitative only).

concepts.name: Physical state trends of small organic molecules
concepts.explanation: Comparing physical state (solid/liquid/gas) of small alkanes/alcohols/aldehydes/acids as a physical property outcome of intermolecular forces.

concepts.name: Structural comparison of alcohols with water
concepts.explanation: Comparing the presence of an -OH group in alcohols with water to rationalize similarities such as hydrogen-bonding-related properties (qualitatively).

concepts.name: Solubility comparison: methanol vs butan-1-ol in water and cyclohexane
concepts.explanation: Practical/qualitative comparison showing shorter-chain alcohols are more water-soluble, while longer-chain alcohols show increased solubility in non-polar solvents.

concepts.name: Solubility test: ethanal in water vs cyclohexane
concepts.explanation: Qualitative determination/comparison of ethanal solubility in a polar solvent (water) versus a non-polar solvent (cyclohexane).

concepts.name: Solubility test: ethanoic acid in water vs cyclohexane
concepts.explanation: Qualitative determination/comparison of ethanoic acid solubility in water and in cyclohexane to illustrate strong polarity effects.

concepts.name: Solubility test: methylbenzene in water vs cyclohexane
concepts.explanation: Qualitative comparison showing methylbenzene is much more soluble in non-polar cyclohexane than in water.

concepts.name: Benzene bonding representation using a circle
concepts.explanation: Using a circle in the benzene ring to indicate identical C–C bonds intermediate between single and double bonds (delocalization idea, qualitatively).

concepts.name: Aromatic compounds: defining features (structures not required)
concepts.explanation: Awareness of aromatic chemistry scope and that aromatic compounds commonly contain benzene-ring systems, without requiring detailed structures.

concepts.name: Unreactivity of benzene toward addition reactions (relative to ethene)
concepts.explanation: Benzene does not readily undergo addition reactions compared with alkenes such as ethene, reflecting aromatic stabilization (qualitative).

concepts.name: Addition reactions of alkenes (general type)
concepts.explanation: Reactions where atoms add across the C=C bond of an alkene, converting a double bond to single bonds and forming new products.

concepts.name: Hydrogenation of alkenes (addition of hydrogen)
concepts.explanation: Addition of H2 across an alkene double bond to form an alkane; also applied industrially to hydrogenate vegetable oils.

concepts.name: Halogen addition to alkenes (chlorine and bromine)
concepts.explanation: Addition of Cl2 or Br2 across a C=C bond to form dihaloalkanes, written using balanced structural equations.

concepts.name: Hydration of alkenes (addition of water)
concepts.explanation: Addition of H and OH across a C=C bond to form an alcohol (treated as an addition reaction written with structural formulas).

concepts.name: Addition of hydrogen chloride to alkenes
concepts.explanation: Addition of HCl across a C=C bond to form a chloroalkane, represented with balanced equations using structural formulas.

concepts.name: Polymerisation of ethene and propene (addition polymerisation)
concepts.explanation: Formation of polymers from ethene or propene by addition polymerisation (mechanism not required).

concepts.name: Substitution reactions: halogenation of alkanes
concepts.explanation: A reaction where a hydrogen atom in an alkane is replaced by a halogen atom (treated as a substitution reaction type).

concepts.name: Elimination reactions: dehydration of alcohols
concepts.explanation: Removal of water from an alcohol to form an alkene (classified as an elimination reaction).

concepts.name: Oxidation of alcohols to aldehydes and acids (KMnO4 or Na2Cr2O7)
concepts.explanation: Using oxidising agents (permanganate or dichromate) to oxidise alcohols to aldehydes and further to carboxylic acids; half-equations only required.

concepts.name: Oxidation of aldehydes to carboxylic acids
concepts.explanation: Aldehydes can be oxidised to carboxylic acids; representation may use half-equations at this level.

concepts.name: Combustion of organic compounds
concepts.explanation: Combustion is a common reaction of most organic compounds, producing CO2 and H2O in complete combustion.

concepts.name: Combustion of alcohols
concepts.explanation: Alcohols burn in oxygen to form carbon dioxide and water; equations can be written and balanced using structural/molecular formulas.

concepts.name: Non-flammability of fully halogenated alkanes
concepts.explanation: Alkanes in which all hydrogens are replaced by halogens are described as non-flammable in the syllabus context.

concepts.name: Balanced structural equations for organic reactions
concepts.explanation: Writing balanced chemical equations using structural formulas for specified organic reaction types.
concepts.broader_concept: Representations and equations in organic chemistry

concepts.name: Fermentation as a source of ethanol
concepts.explanation: Production of ethanol via fermentation (biochemical conversion), linked to brewing and distilling applications.
concepts.broader_concept: Industrial and biological sources of organic chemicals

concepts.name: Ethanol as a solvent
concepts.explanation: Use of ethanol as a solvent, reflecting its intermediate polarity relative to water and non-polar solvents.

concepts.name: Methanol as a denaturing agent
concepts.explanation: Methanol is used to denature ethanol (render it unsuitable for consumption) in industrial/alcohol supply contexts.

concepts.name: Organic compounds as fuels (alcohols and hydrocarbons)
concepts.explanation: Use of organic substances (e.g., alcohols) as fuels due to energy released on combustion.

concepts.name: Organic synthesis as bond breaking and bond forming
concepts.explanation: Chemical synthesis is understood in terms of breaking existing covalent bonds and forming new covalent bonds to create target organic molecules/materials.

concepts.name: Synthesis of PVC from ethene (addition polymerisation route)
concepts.explanation: An example synthetic route where ethene is converted via appropriate intermediates to poly(chloroethene) (PVC); requires the reaction sequence and structural representations.

concepts.name: Alcohols reacting as acids with sodium
concepts.explanation: Alcohols can act as weak acids and react with sodium metal to form sodium alkoxides and hydrogen gas.

concepts.name: Carboxylic acids reacting with magnesium
concepts.explanation: Carboxylic acids act as acids and react with magnesium to form a magnesium carboxylate salt and hydrogen gas.

concepts.name: Carboxylic acids reacting with sodium hydroxide
concepts.explanation: Neutralisation reaction: carboxylic acid + sodium hydroxide produces a sodium carboxylate salt and water.

concepts.name: Carboxylic acids reacting with sodium carbonate
concepts.explanation: Acid-carbonate reaction: carboxylic acid + sodium carbonate produces a sodium carboxylate salt, carbon dioxide, and water.

concepts.name: Extraction by solvent extraction
concepts.explanation: Separation technique where a compound is partitioned between immiscible solvents to isolate desired organic components from a mixture.

concepts.name: Extraction by steam distillation
concepts.explanation: Technique for isolating volatile, water-immiscible organic compounds (e.g., essential oils) by co-distillation with steam at reduced effective boiling temperature.

concepts.name: Petrochemical industry producing synthetic products
concepts.explanation: Awareness that the petrochemical industry converts petroleum fractions into a wide range of synthetic chemicals and materials (students provide examples).

concepts.name: Industrial manufacture of plastics (materials in manufacture)
concepts.explanation: Understanding that specific raw materials/feedstocks are used industrially to manufacture plastics, linked to petrochemical sources.

concepts.name: Soap manufacture
concepts.explanation: Production of soap from fats/oils via saponification, yielding soap (salts of fatty acids) and glycerol.

concepts.name: Ethanal formation in ethanol metabolism
concepts.explanation: In the human body, ethanol is oxidised during metabolism to ethanal (acetaldehyde) as a key intermediate product.

concepts.name: Alcohols as motor fuels
concepts.explanation: Use of alcohols (e.g., ethanol) as fuels or fuel additives in engines, relating chemical properties of alcohols to combustion and energy use.

concepts.name: Flame retardants (chemical role)
concepts.explanation: Substances added to materials to reduce flammability by interfering with combustion processes (e.g., radical quenching, forming protective layers).

concepts.name: Fire extinguishers (chemical basis)
concepts.explanation: Chemical principles behind extinguishing fires, such as removing oxygen, cooling, or inhibiting combustion reactions depending on extinguisher type.

concepts.name: Organic natural products: useful examples and scope
concepts.explanation: Recognition that many useful substances are organic natural products; students can identify examples without needing structural detail.

concepts.name: Useful products of organic synthesis (examples such as aspirin or paracetamol)
concepts.explanation: Recognition that organic synthesis yields useful pharmaceuticals; students can name examples without requiring structures or full synthetic routes.

concepts.name: Chromatography
concepts.explanation: A separation technique where a mixture is carried by a mobile phase and moves in contact with a selectively absorbent stationary phase, causing components to separate based on differing interactions with the phases.

concepts.name: Mobile phase (chromatography)
concepts.explanation: The moving phase in chromatography that carries the mixture through or over the stationary phase.

concepts.name: Stationary phase (chromatography)
concepts.explanation: The non-moving, selectively absorbent phase in chromatography that interacts with mixture components and enables separation.

concepts.name: Thin-layer chromatography (TLC)
concepts.explanation: A chromatography method using a thin layer of adsorbent material as the stationary phase to separate components of a mixture.

concepts.name: TLC separation of dyes from fibres (forensic application)
concepts.explanation: A practical procedure using TLC to separate dye mixtures extracted from fibres to support forensic comparison and identification.

concepts.name: Gas chromatography (GC)
concepts.explanation: An instrumental separation technique where a gas mobile phase carries volatile components through a column for separation.

concepts.name: High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC)
concepts.explanation: An instrumental separation technique using a liquid mobile phase forced under high pressure through a column to separate mixture components efficiently.

concepts.name: Mass spectrometry (as an analytical method)
concepts.explanation: An instrumental analytical technique used to obtain information about substances by producing and detecting ions; emphasis on basic principle rather than detailed spectral interpretation.

concepts.name: Recrystallisation (purification by recrystallisation)
concepts.explanation: Purification technique where an impure solid is dissolved in a suitable hot solvent and purified crystals form on cooling, leaving impurities in solution.

concepts.name: Melting point determination (benzoic acid)
concepts.explanation: Measuring the melting point of a solid to assess purity (sharp melting point indicates higher purity) and to help identify the substance.

concepts.name: Soap preparation (saponification)
concepts.explanation: Preparation of soap by alkaline hydrolysis of fats/oils (triglycerides) to produce fatty acid salts (soap) and glycerol.
concepts.broader_concept: Organic reactions of esters and fats

concepts.name: Ethene preparation
concepts.explanation: Laboratory preparation of ethene as an alkene (commonly via dehydration of an alcohol) and collection of the gas.

concepts.name: Combustion of ethene
concepts.explanation: Oxidation reaction of ethene with oxygen to form carbon dioxide and water; used to demonstrate combustion properties of hydrocarbons/alkenes.

concepts.name: Test for unsaturation using bromine water
concepts.explanation: Qualitative test where bromine water is decolourised by alkenes due to addition across the C=C bond, indicating unsaturation.

concepts.name: Test for unsaturation using acidified potassium manganate(VII)
concepts.explanation: Qualitative test where acidified KMnO4 is decolourised (and can form oxidation products) in the presence of C=C bonds, indicating unsaturation.

concepts.name: Ethanal preparation
concepts.explanation: Laboratory preparation of ethanal (an aldehyde), commonly by controlled oxidation of ethanol and distillation to prevent further oxidation.
concepts.broader_concept: Organic synthesis and oxidation of alcohols

concepts.name: Oxidation of ethanal with acidified potassium manganate(VII)
concepts.explanation: Reaction demonstrating that aldehydes are readily oxidised (ethanal oxidises to ethanoic acid) with acidified KMnO4 as the oxidant.

concepts.name: Fehling's test for aldehydes
concepts.explanation: Aldehydes reduce Fehling’s solution (Cu2+ complex) to brick-red Cu2O precipitate, distinguishing aldehydes from many ketones.

concepts.name: Tollens' test (ammoniacal silver nitrate) for aldehydes
concepts.explanation: Aldehydes reduce [Ag(NH3)2]+ to metallic silver (silver mirror), serving as a qualitative test for aldehydes.

concepts.name: Ethanoic acid preparation
concepts.explanation: Laboratory preparation of ethanoic acid (a carboxylic acid), commonly by oxidation of ethanol or ethanal under appropriate conditions.

concepts.name: Reaction of ethanoic acid with sodium carbonate
concepts.explanation: Acid-carbonate reaction producing sodium ethanoate, carbon dioxide and water; used to demonstrate acidic properties of carboxylic acids.

concepts.name: Reaction of ethanoic acid with magnesium
concepts.explanation: Acid-metal reaction producing magnesium ethanoate and hydrogen gas; demonstrates acidity and salt formation by carboxylic acids.

concepts.name: Steam distillation (extraction of clove oil)
concepts.explanation: Separation/extraction method for volatile, heat-sensitive organic compounds using co-distillation with water steam to lower effective boiling temperature.
concepts.broader_concept: Separation and purification of organic compounds

concepts.name: Paper chromatography (separation of indicators)
concepts.explanation: Chromatographic technique using paper as the stationary phase to separate components of a mixture based on differing affinities for stationary/mobile phases.

concepts.name: Thin-layer chromatography (TLC) (separation of indicators)
concepts.explanation: Chromatographic technique using a thin adsorbent layer (e.g., silica) as stationary phase to separate mixture components; commonly used for identification/purity checks.

concepts.name: Column chromatography (separation of indicators)
concepts.explanation: Preparative chromatographic method where a mixture is passed through an adsorbent-packed column to separate components by different adsorption/elution rates.

concepts.name: Trace organic pollutant analysis in water
concepts.explanation: Analytical chemistry application focusing on detecting and measuring low concentrations of organic contaminants in water samples.
concepts.broader_concept: Environmental and analytical applications of organic chemistry

concepts.name: Analysis of gases from a waste dump
concepts.explanation: Sampling and analysis of landfill/waste dump gases to determine composition and potential pollutants (qualitative/quantitative gas analysis application).

concepts.name: Blood alcohol testing (ethanol analysis)
concepts.explanation: Analytical determination of ethanol in blood as an application of chemical testing and quantification in real-world contexts.

concepts.name: Drug testing in athletes (trace organic analysis)
concepts.explanation: Detection and identification of drug compounds and/or metabolites in biological samples using analytical methods.

concepts.name: Dynamic equilibrium in reversible reactions
concepts.explanation: In a reversible reaction, equilibrium is dynamic: forward and reverse reactions continue to occur simultaneously in a closed system.

concepts.name: Equal forward and reverse reaction rates at equilibrium
concepts.explanation: At equilibrium, the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction, so macroscopic concentrations remain constant.

concepts.name: Equilibrium law (expression for Kc)
concepts.explanation: For a reaction at equilibrium, Kc is written using equilibrium concentrations of products over reactants, each raised to their stoichiometric coefficients.

concepts.name: Equilibrium constant Kc
concepts.explanation: Kc is a constant value at a fixed temperature that quantifies the equilibrium position for a given reaction using concentrations.

concepts.name: Le Chatelier’s principle
concepts.explanation: If a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it shifts in the direction that tends to oppose the disturbance and re-establish equilibrium.

concepts.name: Effect of concentration changes on equilibrium position
concepts.explanation: Changing reactant or product concentration causes the equilibrium position to shift to reduce the effect of the concentration change.

concepts.name: Effect of pressure changes on equilibrium position
concepts.explanation: For gaseous equilibria, changing pressure (or volume) shifts equilibrium toward the side with fewer moles of gas to counter the change.

concepts.name: Effect of temperature changes on equilibrium position
concepts.explanation: Temperature changes shift equilibrium depending on reaction enthalpy: heating favors the endothermic direction, cooling favors the exothermic direction.

concepts.name: Effect of a catalyst on equilibrium position
concepts.explanation: A catalyst increases the rates of both forward and reverse reactions but does not change the equilibrium position; it only helps equilibrium be reached faster.

concepts.name: Equilibrium shift illustrated by cobalt(II) chloride complex equilibrium
concepts.explanation: The equilibrium CoCl4^2− + 6H2O ⇌ [Co(H2O)6]^2+ + 4Cl− can be shifted by changing temperature or chloride/water concentration, producing observable color changes.
concepts.broader_concept: Experimental demonstrations of Le Chatelier’s principle

concepts.name: Equilibrium shift illustrated by dichromate–chromate equilibrium
concepts.explanation: The dichromate/chromate equilibrium (e.g., Cr2O7^2− ⇌ 2CrO4^2− in acid/base conditions) demonstrates concentration-dependent equilibrium shifts with visible color change.
concepts.broader_concept: Experimental demonstrations of Le Chatelier’s principle

concepts.name: Equilibrium shift illustrated by iron(III) thiocyanate complex formation
concepts.explanation: The equilibrium Fe^3+ + SCN− ⇌ FeSCN^2+ shows how changing reactant concentrations shifts equilibrium, observed via intensity changes in the red complex color.
concepts.broader_concept: Experimental demonstrations of Le Chatelier’s principle

concepts.name: Industrial application of Le Chatelier’s principle: Contact process equilibrium
concepts.explanation: In the Contact process, conditions are chosen for 2SO2(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2SO3(g) to favor yield while maintaining a practical reaction rate (temperature, pressure, catalyst).

concepts.name: Industrial application of Le Chatelier’s principle: Haber process equilibrium
concepts.explanation: In the Haber process, conditions are selected for N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g) to balance equilibrium yield with reaction rate using pressure, temperature and catalyst.

concepts.name: pH scale
concepts.explanation: A logarithmic scale used to express acidity/alkalinity of aqueous solutions based on hydrogen ion concentration.
concepts.broader_concept: Acids and bases in aqueous solution

concepts.name: Universal indicator (paper/solution) for pH estimation
concepts.explanation: Use of a mixed indicator to estimate pH by comparing the observed colour to a reference colour chart.

concepts.name: Limitations of the pH scale (dilute aqueous solutions)
concepts.explanation: Recognition that pH is most useful for dilute aqueous solutions and is less meaningful for concentrated solutions or non-aqueous systems.

concepts.name: Calculation of pH for dilute strong acids
concepts.explanation: Determining pH from the hydrogen ion concentration of a dilute strong acid assuming complete dissociation.

concepts.name: Calculation of pH for dilute strong bases
concepts.explanation: Determining pH (via pOH) from hydroxide ion concentration of a dilute strong base assuming complete dissociation.

concepts.name: Hardness in water
concepts.explanation: Water quality property caused mainly by dissolved calcium and magnesium ions that reduces lathering and forms scale.

concepts.name: Temporary hardness
concepts.explanation: Hardness primarily due to dissolved hydrogencarbonates of calcium/magnesium, removable by boiling.

concepts.name: Permanent hardness
concepts.explanation: Hardness due to dissolved calcium/magnesium sulfates (and related salts), not removed by boiling.

concepts.name: Deionisation of water
concepts.explanation: Removal of dissolved ions from water, commonly using ion-exchange resins to produce deionised water.

concepts.name: Testing scale deposits in a kettle
concepts.explanation: Simple chemical testing/observation of kettle scale to infer hardness-related deposits (typically calcium carbonate).

concepts.name: Removal of hardness by boiling
concepts.explanation: Reduction of temporary hardness by heating, which converts soluble hydrogencarbonates to insoluble carbonates (scale).

concepts.name: Removal of hardness by ion exchange
concepts.explanation: Use of ion-exchange resins to replace Ca2+/Mg2+ with other ions (commonly Na+), softening water.

concepts.name: Water treatment: sedimentation
concepts.explanation: Process step where suspended solids settle under gravity to clarify water before further treatment.

concepts.name: Water treatment: flocculation
concepts.explanation: Aggregation of fine particles into larger flocs (often aided by coagulants) to improve removal by settling/filtration.

concepts.name: Water treatment: filtration
concepts.explanation: Removal of suspended particles by passing water through filter media (e.g., sand filters).

concepts.name: Water treatment: chlorination
concepts.explanation: Disinfection of water using chlorine/chlorine compounds to kill microorganisms and maintain a residual disinfectant.

concepts.name: Water treatment: fluoridation
concepts.explanation: Controlled addition of fluoride compounds to drinking water to reduce tooth decay.

concepts.name: Water treatment: pH adjustment
concepts.explanation: Chemical dosing to alter pH for corrosion control, disinfection effectiveness, and overall water stability.

concepts.name: Primary sewage treatment
concepts.explanation: Physical removal of large solids and settleable matter using processes such as screening and settlement.

concepts.name: Secondary sewage treatment (bacterial breakdown)
concepts.explanation: Biological treatment where microorganisms decompose organic matter, reducing biochemical oxygen demand.

concepts.name: Tertiary sewage treatment (phosphate and nitrate reduction)
concepts.explanation: Advanced treatment to lower nutrient levels (especially phosphates and nitrates) to reduce environmental impact.

concepts.name: Nutrients and eutrophication
concepts.explanation: Understanding how elevated nitrate and phosphate levels promote algal blooms and oxygen depletion in water bodies.

concepts.name: Regulatory limits for chemical species in water (EU limits)
concepts.explanation: Awareness that drinking/environmental waters have legal concentration limits for specific chemical species such as nitrates, phosphates, and certain metal ions.

concepts.name: pH meter (principle of instrumental pH measurement)
concepts.explanation: Instrumental determination of pH using an electrode system that relates measured potential to hydrogen ion activity.

concepts.name: Colorimetry (principle)
concepts.explanation: Quantitative analysis based on measuring light absorbance of coloured solutions to determine concentration.

concepts.name: Qualitative tests for anions in aqueous solution
concepts.explanation: Systematic chemical tests used to identify anions in water samples (e.g., precipitation or gas evolution tests).

concepts.name: Colorimetric estimation of free chlorine
concepts.explanation: Using a colorimeter/comparator with a suitable reagent to estimate free chlorine concentration in pool water or bleach.

concepts.name: Determination of total suspended solids (TSS) by filtration
concepts.explanation: Measuring suspended solids in water by filtering a known volume and quantifying the retained residue, typically reported in ppm.

concepts.name: Determination of total dissolved solids (TDS) by evaporation
concepts.explanation: Measuring dissolved solids by evaporating a known volume of filtrate and quantifying the remaining residue, typically reported in ppm.

concepts.name: Reporting concentrations in parts per million (ppm) for water analysis
concepts.explanation: Expressing low concentrations of solutes or solids in water as ppm, commonly approximated as mg L^-1 for dilute aqueous systems.

concepts.name: Organic chemical pollutants in water (sources)
concepts.explanation: Identification of organic pollution sources such as sewage, industrial waste, silage, and milk that can contaminate water bodies.

concepts.name: Batch industrial chemical process
concepts.explanation: An industrial production method where reactants are charged to a vessel, processed for a set time, and products are removed before the next cycle.

concepts.name: Continuous industrial chemical process
concepts.explanation: An industrial production method where reactants are continuously fed into a process and products are continuously removed during operation.

concepts.name: Semi-continuous (semi-batch) industrial chemical process
concepts.explanation: An industrial process combining batch and continuous features, where some materials are added or removed continuously while other steps occur in batches.

concepts.name: Feedstock (raw materials) in industrial chemical processes
concepts.explanation: The raw material(s) supplied to an industrial chemical process, selected based on availability, cost, purity, and suitability for the desired products.
concepts.broader_concept: Characteristics of effective industrial chemical processes

concepts.name: Characteristics of an effective industrial chemical process
concepts.explanation: Criteria used to judge industrial process success (e.g., appropriate feedstock choice and other performance factors), focusing on efficiency and practicality at scale.

concepts.name: Effect of pressure on reaction rate (gas-phase reactions)
concepts.explanation: How increasing pressure in gas-phase systems increases concentration of gases and can increase reaction rate by raising collision frequency.

concepts.name: Catalyst effect on reaction rate
concepts.explanation: How a catalyst increases reaction rate by providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy without being consumed overall.

concepts.name: Effect of temperature on product yield in industrial processes
concepts.explanation: How reaction temperature influences product yield, often through equilibrium position and/or side reactions, and the need to balance yield with rate.

concepts.name: Effect of pressure on product yield in industrial processes
concepts.explanation: How changing pressure affects product yield, especially for reactions involving gases, commonly via shifts in equilibrium toward fewer/more moles of gas.

concepts.name: Catalyst effect on product yield (selectivity)
concepts.explanation: How catalysts can increase the yield of a desired product by improving selectivity and reducing formation of unwanted by-products.

concepts.name: Separation of co-products in industrial chemical processes
concepts.explanation: Techniques used to separate multiple products formed in a process (e.g., distillation, filtration, extraction) to obtain useful co-products and purify main product.

concepts.name: Industrial waste water treatment
concepts.explanation: Processes for treating aqueous effluent from chemical plants to remove contaminants before discharge or reuse (e.g., neutralization, precipitation, biological treatment).

concepts.name: Emission control in industrial chemistry
concepts.explanation: Methods for controlling gaseous and particulate emissions from industrial processes (e.g., scrubbers, filters, catalytic converters) to reduce environmental impact.

concepts.name: Quality control in chemical manufacturing
concepts.explanation: Monitoring and testing raw materials, intermediates, and final products to ensure composition, purity, and performance meet specifications.

concepts.name: Hazard monitoring and safety features in chemical plants
concepts.explanation: Identifying and monitoring hazards (e.g., toxic releases, fire, explosion risk) and using engineered safety features and procedures to reduce risk.

concepts.name: Cost reduction by heat exchangers in chemical processes
concepts.explanation: Using heat exchangers to recover and reuse heat within a plant to lower energy consumption and operating costs.

concepts.name: Recycling unreacted materials to reduce process costs
concepts.explanation: Returning unreacted reactants or solvents back into the process stream to increase overall efficiency and reduce raw material costs and waste.

concepts.name: Corrosion resistance of chemical plant construction materials
concepts.explanation: Selection of materials for chemical plant equipment based on resistance to chemical attack and corrosion in service environments.

concepts.name: Chemically unreactive materials for chemical plant construction
concepts.explanation: Use of chemically inert or low-reactivity materials to prevent unwanted reactions between process chemicals and plant equipment.

concepts.name: Chemistry contribution to provision of pure water
concepts.explanation: How chemical processes enable purification of water for safe use (e.g., treatment and removal of contaminants).

concepts.name: Chemistry contribution to fuels
concepts.explanation: Role of chemistry in producing and improving fuels for energy applications.

concepts.name: Chemistry contribution to metals
concepts.explanation: How chemistry enables extraction, purification, and processing of metals for societal use.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Chemistry contribution to medicines
concepts.explanation: Use of chemical knowledge and synthesis to develop pharmaceuticals and medicinal products.

concepts.name: Chemistry contribution to detergents
concepts.explanation: How chemical formulation produces detergents and cleaning agents with desired properties.

concepts.name: Chemistry contribution to enzymes
concepts.explanation: Role of chemistry in understanding and using enzymes in industrial and societal applications.

concepts.name: Chemistry contribution to dyes and paints
concepts.explanation: How chemical structure and formulation lead to dyes and paints with specific color and performance properties.

concepts.name: Chemistry contribution to semiconductors
concepts.explanation: Chemical principles and materials chemistry involved in producing semiconductor materials used in electronics.

concepts.name: Chemistry contribution to liquid crystals
concepts.explanation: Use of chemical design and materials chemistry to produce liquid-crystal substances used in displays and related technologies.

concepts.name: Haber process (ammonia manufacture from natural gas, steam and air)
concepts.explanation: Industrial synthesis of ammonia using hydrogen (derived from natural gas and water vapour) and nitrogen (from air), typically over an iron catalyst under high temperature and pressure.

concepts.name: Balanced equation for ammonia formation
concepts.explanation: Stoichiometric chemical equation for ammonia synthesis: N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3, including correct balancing of atoms.
concepts.broader_concept: Writing and balancing industrial reaction equations

concepts.name: Industrial conversion of ammonia to urea
concepts.explanation: Use of ammonia as a feedstock to produce urea (a nitrogen fertiliser), typically via reaction with carbon dioxide under industrial conditions.

concepts.name: Ostwald process (nitric acid manufacture from ammonia)
concepts.explanation: Industrial production of nitric acid starting from ammonia, involving catalytic oxidation steps leading to nitric acid formation.

concepts.name: Balanced equation for oxidation of nitrogen monoxide
concepts.explanation: Stoichiometric equation for a key Ostwald step: 2NO + O2 → 2NO2, correctly balanced.
concepts.broader_concept: Writing and balancing industrial reaction equations

concepts.name: Nitric acid use in fertiliser manufacture
concepts.explanation: Application of nitric acid as a reactant to produce nitrate-based fertilisers (e.g., ammonium nitrate), linking industrial acids to agricultural chemicals.

concepts.name: Manufacture of magnesium oxide from sea water
concepts.explanation: Industrial extraction of magnesium compounds from seawater followed by conversion to magnesium oxide as a commercial product.
concepts.broader_concept: Industrial production of inorganic materials from natural sources

concepts.name: Balanced equation for magnesium oxide formation
concepts.explanation: Chemical equation representing formation of MgO from a magnesium-containing precursor and oxygen, with correct stoichiometric balancing.
concepts.broader_concept: Writing and balancing industrial reaction equations

concepts.name: Magnesium oxide as a refractory (heat-resistant) material
concepts.explanation: Use of MgO for furnace linings due to its high melting point and thermal stability (refractory properties).

concepts.name: Chemical industry site visit as structured learning activity
concepts.explanation: Planned educational visit to a chemical plant with defined objectives and observations to connect industrial processes to syllabus principles.
concepts.broader_concept: Industrial chemistry fieldwork and process-context learning

concepts.name: Fractional distillation of liquid air to obtain oxygen
concepts.explanation: Separation of air components by liquefying air and using fractional distillation to collect oxygen based on different boiling points.

concepts.name: Atmospheric abundance of nitrogen
concepts.explanation: Nitrogen as the major component of air and the idea of its high atmospheric proportion.

concepts.name: Structure and inertness of nitrogen (N2)
concepts.explanation: Nitrogen gas exists as diatomic N2 and is relatively unreactive under normal conditions due to strong bonding.

concepts.name: Natural nitrogen fixation
concepts.explanation: Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into nitrogen-containing compounds by natural processes (e.g., biological fixation and lightning).

concepts.name: Formation of nitrogen oxides in an electric discharge
concepts.explanation: Reaction of nitrogen and oxygen under high-energy conditions (e.g., lightning) producing nitrogen oxides.

concepts.name: Nitrogen cycle
concepts.explanation: Cyclic movement of nitrogen between atmosphere, biosphere and geosphere through fixation, assimilation, nitrification, and denitrification (overview level).

concepts.name: Combustion of carbon producing CO and CO2
concepts.explanation: Oxidation of carbon can yield carbon monoxide (limited oxygen) or carbon dioxide (excess oxygen).

concepts.name: Carbon monoxide as a neutral oxide
concepts.explanation: Classification of CO as a neutral oxide (does not form acids or bases readily with water).

concepts.name: Carbon dioxide as an acidic oxide
concepts.explanation: Classification of CO2 as an acidic oxide; dissolves in water to form acidic solutions (carbonic acid).

concepts.name: Fermentation as a source of carbon dioxide in ethanol production
concepts.explanation: CO2 is produced during fermentation when sugars are converted to ethanol and carbon dioxide.

concepts.name: Carbon cycle
concepts.explanation: Cyclic transfer of carbon among atmosphere, oceans, living organisms and rocks via processes such as respiration, combustion, photosynthesis and dissolution.

concepts.name: Effect of carbon dioxide on universal indicator (experiment)
concepts.explanation: Demonstration that dissolving CO2 in water lowers pH, shown by a universal indicator color change.

concepts.name: Carbon monoxide toxicity
concepts.explanation: CO is poisonous; exposure risk is associated with incomplete combustion sources such as cigarette smoke and vehicle exhaust.

concepts.name: Greenhouse effect
concepts.explanation: Warming of Earth due to absorption and re-emission of infrared radiation by greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.

concepts.name: Relative greenhouse effects of CO2 and water vapour
concepts.explanation: Comparison of greenhouse gases with emphasis on carbon dioxide and water vapour as major contributors (qualitative).

concepts.name: Ocean dissolution as a sink for atmospheric carbon dioxide
concepts.explanation: Reduction of atmospheric CO2 levels by dissolving in the ocean (concept of ocean uptake).

concepts.name: Sources of nitrogen oxides and sulfur oxides in air pollution
concepts.explanation: Identification of natural, domestic, industrial and internal combustion engine sources of NOx and SOx pollutants.

concepts.name: Formation of acids from dissolved NO2 and SO2
concepts.explanation: Nitrogen dioxide and sulfur dioxide dissolve in water to form acids, contributing to acidified precipitation.

concepts.name: Effect of sulfur dioxide on universal indicator (experiment)
concepts.explanation: Demonstration that SO2 dissolved in water produces an acidic solution, indicated by a universal indicator color change.

concepts.name: Acid rain and environmental effects
