concepts.explanation: Acid rain results from atmospheric acids and harms ecosystems and built environments (qualitative effects).

concepts.name: Scrubbing of waste gases using limestone
concepts.explanation: Removal of acidic gases (notably SO2) from flue emissions by reaction/neutralization with limestone.

concepts.name: Preparation of chloroalkanes by chlorination of alkanes
concepts.explanation: Formation of chloroalkanes via substitution reactions such as chlorination of methane.

concepts.name: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and ozone depletion
concepts.explanation: CFCs are linked to damage of the ozone layer; concept includes their role as major contributors to ozone depletion (qualitative).

concepts.name: Formation of ozone in the stratosphere
concepts.explanation: Ozone is formed in the stratosphere through photochemical processes involving oxygen (qualitative overview).

concepts.name: Beneficial role of the ozone layer
concepts.explanation: The ozone layer protects life by absorbing harmful ultraviolet radiation.

concepts.name: CFCs and HCFCs (classification and uses)
concepts.explanation: Distinguishing CFCs and HCFCs as halogenated hydrocarbons and knowing representative uses of CFCs.

concepts.name: Effects of ozone layer damage
concepts.explanation: Consequences of ozone depletion (e.g., increased UV reaching Earth) and associated impacts (qualitative).

concepts.name: Types of crystals: ionic, molecular, metallic and covalent macromolecular
concepts.explanation: Classification of crystalline solids by bonding/structure type: ionic, molecular, metallic, and covalent network (macromolecular).

concepts.name: Crystal physical properties linked to binding forces
concepts.explanation: How properties such as melting point, hardness and conductivity relate to the strength/type of forces in different crystals.

concepts.name: X-ray crystallography (principle of determining crystal structure)
concepts.explanation: Crystal structures can be determined by scattering of X-rays by a crystal lattice (non-mathematical treatment).

concepts.name: Addition polymers and monomers
concepts.explanation: Definition of addition polymers and monomers; polymers formed by addition of many alkene monomers.

concepts.name: Addition polymerisation of alkenes
concepts.explanation: Reaction process where alkene monomers join to form polymers (e.g., ethene to poly(ethene)).

concepts.name: Low-density poly(ethene) production (polymer from ethene)
concepts.explanation: Formation of low-density poly(ethene) as an example of an addition polymer produced from ethene.

concepts.name: Poly(chloroethene) (PVC) as an addition polymer
concepts.explanation: Polymer made by addition polymerisation of chloroethene (vinyl chloride).

concepts.name: Poly(phenylethene) (polystyrene) as an addition polymer
concepts.explanation: Polymer made by addition polymerisation of phenylethene (styrene).

concepts.name: Comparing polymer physical properties (density, flexibility, hardness)
concepts.explanation: Observation/measurement-based comparison of physical properties of common plastics such as poly(ethene), PVC and polystyrene.

concepts.name: Recycling process for polystyrene
concepts.explanation: Stages of recycling polystyrene: sorting, shredding, washing, drying and re-extrusion.

concepts.name: Physical properties of metals vs non-metals
concepts.explanation: Comparison of characteristic physical properties distinguishing metals and non-metals, including hardness, lustre, malleability, ductility, and thermal/electrical conductivity.
concepts.broader_concept: Classification of elements by physical properties

concepts.name: Thermal conductivity in metals and non-metals
concepts.explanation: Metals typically conduct heat well, while non-metals are generally poorer thermal conductors; used as a distinguishing physical property.

concepts.name: Electrical conductivity in metals and non-metals
concepts.explanation: Metals are typically good electrical conductors whereas most non-metals are insulators; conductivity is a key property for classification and applications.

concepts.name: Malleability as a property of metals
concepts.explanation: Ability of a material (commonly metals) to be hammered or rolled into sheets without breaking.

concepts.name: Ductility as a property of metals
concepts.explanation: Ability of a material (commonly metals) to be drawn into wires without breaking.

concepts.name: Lustre as a characteristic of metals
concepts.explanation: Shiny appearance of metals due to reflection of light from the surface; contrasted with the typically dull appearance of many non-metals.
concepts.broader_concept: Surface and optical properties of materials

concepts.name: Hardness comparison between metals and non-metals
concepts.explanation: Use of hardness as a physical property to compare metals and non-metals, noting that hardness varies widely across both groups.
concepts.broader_concept: Mechanical properties used in material classification

concepts.name: Alloy
concepts.explanation: A material made by combining a metal with one or more other elements to modify properties such as strength, hardness, or corrosion resistance.

concepts.name: Steel as an alloy of iron and carbon
concepts.explanation: Steel is an iron-based alloy containing carbon as a key alloying element.

concepts.name: Effect of carbon content on steel hardness
concepts.explanation: Increasing carbon in steel generally increases hardness (and often strength) by changing the alloy's internal structure and resistance to deformation.

concepts.name: Electrochemical series
concepts.explanation: An ordering of metals by their relative tendency to lose electrons (be oxidised), used to predict relative reactivity and cell voltages.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Simple cell voltage depends on metal combination
concepts.explanation: Different pairs of metals used as electrodes in a simple cell produce different potential differences due to differing tendencies to oxidise/reduce.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolysis of molten lead(II) bromide (experiment)
concepts.explanation: Electrolysis of molten PbBr2 using inert electrodes to produce lead at the cathode and bromine at the anode.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Inert electrodes in electrolysis
concepts.explanation: Electrodes (e.g., graphite/platinum) that conduct electricity but do not take part chemically in the electrolysis reactions.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Corrosion of metals
concepts.explanation: The gradual oxidation and deterioration of metals due to chemical/electrochemical reactions with the environment.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Relative corrodibility of metals
concepts.explanation: Comparison of how readily different metals corrode, linked to their positions in the electrochemical series and environmental conditions.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Corrosion prevention by protective layer
concepts.explanation: Reducing corrosion by physically isolating a metal from air/water using coatings or surface treatments.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Galvanising
concepts.explanation: Corrosion protection by coating iron/steel with zinc, which acts as a barrier and sacrificial metal.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Surface coating for corrosion prevention
concepts.explanation: Applying paints, polymers, or other coatings to prevent contact between metal and corrosive agents.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Extraction of sodium by electrolysis
concepts.explanation: Obtaining sodium metal by electrolysing molten sodium salts due to sodium's high reactivity (strong electropositivity).
concepts.broader_concept: Electrochemical extraction of highly reactive metals
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Extraction of aluminium by electrolysis
concepts.explanation: Producing aluminium by electrolytic reduction of aluminium compounds because aluminium cannot be extracted by carbon reduction.
concepts.broader_concept: Electrochemical extraction of highly reactive metals
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Recycling of aluminium
concepts.explanation: Recovering aluminium metal from scrap for reuse, typically requiring much less energy than primary extraction.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Transition elements: general chemical properties
concepts.explanation: Characteristic properties of d-block elements such as variable oxidation states and formation of coloured compounds.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Transition metals as catalysts
concepts.explanation: Use of transition metals/ions to increase reaction rates by providing alternative reaction pathways.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Blast furnace iron manufacture (chemical aspects)
concepts.explanation: Key chemical reactions in extracting iron from iron ores in a blast furnace, including reduction of iron oxides and formation of slag.

concepts.name: Steel as an alloy of iron
concepts.explanation: Steel is iron alloyed with controlled amounts of carbon and/or other elements to modify properties such as strength and hardness.

concepts.name: Electric arc process for steel manufacture (outline)
concepts.explanation: Steelmaking route using an electric arc furnace where electrical energy melts metal feed and impurities are removed in staged processing.

concepts.name: Environmental aspects of iron and steel production
concepts.explanation: Environmental impacts from iron/steel manufacture such as energy use, emissions, and waste/by-product management.

concepts.name: Historical contributions to electrochemistry (Galvani, Volta, Davy, Faraday)
concepts.explanation: Key historical developments: bioelectric observations (Galvani), invention of the voltaic pile (Volta), early electrolysis/extraction (Davy), and foundational laws and concepts of electrolysis (Faraday).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Periodic table organization and periodic trends
concepts.explanation: The periodic table arranges elements to show repeating (periodic) trends in physical and chemical properties.

concepts.name: Isotopes
concepts.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element (same Z) with different numbers of neutrons (different A).

concepts.name: Relative atomic mass (Ar) and the 12C scale
concepts.explanation: Relative atomic mass is the weighted mean mass of an element’s atoms relative to 1/12 of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

concepts.name: Calculating relative atomic mass from isotopic abundance
concepts.explanation: Approximate Ar can be calculated as a weighted average using each isotope’s mass number and its percentage abundance (e.g., chlorine).

concepts.name: Atoms, molecules, and ions as particles of matter
concepts.explanation: Matter is composed of particles which may be atoms (neutral), molecules (bonded atoms), or ions (charged particles).

concepts.name: Subatomic particles: proton, neutron, electron (properties and location)
concepts.explanation: Protons and neutrons are in the nucleus with relative masses ~1; electrons are outside the nucleus with much smaller relative mass and negative charge; charges and locations distinguish them.

concepts.name: Main group similarities: alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens, noble gases
concepts.explanation: Elements in the same main group show similar chemical properties due to similar outer electron structures; key groups include alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens, and noble gases.

concepts.name: Arranging elements by relative atomic mass (historical approach)
concepts.explanation: Early periodic classifications arranged elements by increasing relative atomic mass, which sometimes differs from the modern atomic-number-based order.

concepts.name: Alkali metal reactivity with water (Li, Na, K demonstration)
concepts.explanation: Lithium, sodium, and potassium react with water producing alkaline hydroxides and hydrogen; reactivity increases down the group.

concepts.name: Energy levels in atoms
concepts.explanation: Electrons in atoms occupy discrete energy levels; transitions between levels involve absorption or emission of specific energies.

concepts.name: Electron arrangement in main energy levels for elements 1–20
concepts.explanation: For the first 20 elements, electrons fill main energy levels (shells) with characteristic maximum occupancies (e.g., 2, 8, 8...).

concepts.name: Classifying first 20 elements by number of outer (valence) electrons
concepts.explanation: The periodic position of the first twenty elements can be related to the number of electrons in the outermost energy level, linking to group number and chemical behavior.

concepts.name: Emission and absorption spectra of hydrogen (Balmer series)
concepts.explanation: Hydrogen shows line spectra; the Balmer series is a set of visible emission lines arising from electron transitions to a specific energy level.

concepts.name: Line spectra as evidence for discrete energy levels
concepts.explanation: The presence of discrete spectral lines (rather than continuous spectra) indicates quantized electron energy levels in atoms.

concepts.name: Energy sub-levels (subshells)
concepts.explanation: Within main energy levels, electrons occupy sub-levels (e.g., s and p) with different energies and capacities.

concepts.name: Wave nature of the electron (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: Electrons exhibit wave-like behavior, motivating orbital descriptions rather than fixed paths (non-mathematical treatment).

concepts.name: Heisenberg uncertainty principle (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: It is not possible to know both the exact position and exact momentum of an electron simultaneously; supports probabilistic orbitals.

concepts.name: Atomic orbitals and shapes of s and p orbitals
concepts.explanation: Orbitals are regions of high probability for finding electrons; s orbitals are spherical and p orbitals are dumbbell-shaped (directional).

concepts.name: Building up electronic configuration for first 36 elements
concepts.explanation: Electron configurations for elements 1–36 are constructed by filling orbitals in order of increasing energy (qualitative filling order).

concepts.name: Electronic configurations of ions (s- and p-block only)
concepts.explanation: Ions form by loss or gain of electrons; electron configurations of s- and p-block ions reflect these changes and often reach noble-gas configurations.

concepts.name: Electron arrangement within p orbitals (p-block atoms)
concepts.explanation: Electrons occupy individual p orbitals within a p sublevel before pairing, determining electron distributions in p-block atoms (qualitative orbital filling).

concepts.name: Covalent atomic radius and periodic trends
concepts.explanation: Covalent radius (atomic size in covalent bonding) generally increases down a group and decreases across a period for main-group elements, due to shielding and nuclear charge effects.

concepts.name: First ionisation energy and periodic trends (including exceptions)
concepts.explanation: First ionisation energy is the energy required to remove the first electron from a gaseous atom; it shows trends down groups and across periods with specific exceptions explained by sublevel/paired-electron effects.

concepts.name: Successive ionisation energies
concepts.explanation: Second and subsequent ionisation energies are the energies to remove additional electrons from gaseous ions; large jumps indicate removal from a new (inner) energy level.

concepts.name: Using successive ionisation energies as evidence for energy levels
concepts.explanation: Patterns and jumps in successive ionisation energy values provide evidence for electron shells (principal energy levels) in atoms.

concepts.name: Mass spectrometry for determining relative atomic mass
concepts.explanation: Mass spectrometry determines isotopic masses and abundances, allowing calculation of an element’s relative atomic mass.

concepts.name: Mass spectrometer processes: vaporisation, ionisation, acceleration, separation, detection
concepts.explanation: A mass spectrometer works by vaporising a sample, forming positive ions, accelerating them, separating ions by mass/charge, and detecting them to produce a mass spectrum (qualitative steps).

concepts.name: Alpha, beta, and gamma radiation (nature and penetrating ability)
concepts.explanation: Alpha, beta, and gamma are types of nuclear radiation with distinct particles/energy and characteristic penetrating power.

concepts.name: Chemical reactions vs nuclear reactions
concepts.explanation: Chemical reactions involve electron rearrangements, while nuclear reactions involve changes in the nucleus (e.g., alpha and beta emissions) and can be represented by simple nuclear equations.

concepts.name: Detection and shielding demonstration for nuclear radiation
concepts.explanation: Radiation can be detected and its penetrating power compared using suitable detectors and absorbers (e.g., paper/aluminum/lead), without requiring detector mechanism details.

concepts.name: Emission spectra observation using a spectroscope/spectrometer
concepts.explanation: Experimental observation of characteristic line emission spectra from elements using a spectroscope or spectrometer.

concepts.name: Atomic absorption spectrometry (AAS) principle (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: AAS measures absorption of characteristic wavelengths by gaseous atoms; absorption relates to the presence/concentration of specific elements (qualitative overview).

concepts.name: Electrochemical series (reactivity series based on oxidation tendency)
concepts.explanation: A list of metals arranged by their tendency to be oxidised (lose electrons), used to compare relative reactivities.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Metal displacement reaction (redox)
concepts.explanation: A more reactive metal is oxidised and displaces a less reactive metal ion from solution (e.g., Zn + Cu2+).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolysis of copper(II) sulfate solution with copper electrodes
concepts.explanation: Electrolysis setup where copper dissolves at the anode and plates at the cathode; described using half-equations.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolysis of acidified water with inert electrodes
concepts.explanation: Electrolysis producing hydrogen at the cathode and oxygen at the anode; represented using half-equations.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Half-equations for redox reactions
concepts.explanation: Represent oxidation and reduction separately as electron-loss and electron-gain equations (e.g., 2Br− → Br2 + 2e−).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Demonstration of ionic movement in an electric field
concepts.explanation: Show that cations migrate to the cathode and anions migrate to the anode during electrolysis.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolysis of aqueous sodium sulfate using universal indicator
concepts.explanation: Demonstration electrolysis highlighting pH changes near electrodes (acidic near anode, alkaline near cathode).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolysis of aqueous potassium iodide using phenolphthalein
concepts.explanation: Demonstration electrolysis showing hydroxide formation at the cathode (pink with phenolphthalein) and iodine formation at the anode.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Halogens as oxidising agents (Group VII redox)
concepts.explanation: Halogens gain electrons and oxidise other species; their oxidising strength underpins displacement reactions among halides.

concepts.name: Redox reactions of halogens with halide ions
concepts.explanation: Halogen displacement reactions where a more reactive halogen oxidises a halide ion to its halogen (e.g., Br2 oxidises I− to I2).

concepts.name: Chemical properties depend on electronic structure
concepts.explanation: Link element reactivity and properties to electron arrangement (especially valence electrons).

concepts.name: Atomic radius trend explained by nuclear charge and screening
concepts.explanation: Explain changes in atomic radius using effective nuclear charge: increasing nuclear charge contracts radius while screening reduces attraction.

concepts.name: Screening effect (electron shielding)
concepts.explanation: Inner-shell electrons reduce the attractive force of the nucleus on outer electrons, affecting size and reactivity trends.

concepts.name: Nuclear charge and effective nuclear charge
concepts.explanation: Nuclear charge is the positive charge from protons; effective nuclear charge is the net attraction felt by outer electrons after screening.

concepts.name: Group trends in properties for Group I and Group VII
concepts.explanation: Describe and explain general trends in reactivity/properties down Group I and Group VII using radius, screening and nuclear charge ideas.

concepts.name: Rusting of iron as oxidation (corrosion)
concepts.explanation: Corrosion of iron involves oxidation; used as a real-world example of redox processes.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electroplating
concepts.explanation: Use electrolysis to coat an object with a metal layer by reduction of metal ions at the cathode.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Purification of copper by electrolysis
concepts.explanation: Electrolytic refining where impure copper is oxidised at the anode and pure copper is deposited at the cathode.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Use of scrap iron to extract copper from copper(II) solutions
concepts.explanation: Redox displacement where iron is oxidised and copper(II) ions are reduced to copper metal.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Simple chemical formula
concepts.explanation: Representation of a compound using element symbols and subscripts to show the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms/ions present.

concepts.name: Valency as attainment of stable electronic structure
concepts.explanation: Interpreting valency as the combining capacity of an element explained by gaining, losing, or sharing electrons to reach a stable outer shell.

concepts.name: Variable valency of transition elements (Cu, Fe, Cr, Mn)
concepts.explanation: The ability of certain transition metals to form ions/compounds in more than one oxidation state, leading to different formulas and properties.

concepts.name: Predicting formulas of binary compounds using the octet rule
concepts.explanation: Using typical valencies/ion charges guided by the octet rule to determine empirical formulas of two-element compounds (main-group elements).

concepts.name: Writing formulas of hydroxides, carbonates, nitrates, hydrogencarbonates, sulfites and sulfates
concepts.explanation: Constructing correct ionic formulas by combining cations with common polyatomic anions using charge balance.

concepts.name: Uses of helium and argon based on chemical unreactivity
concepts.explanation: Applications of He and Ar that rely on their inertness (e.g., protective atmospheres, lighting, shielding gases).

concepts.name: Relative size of ions
concepts.explanation: Understanding that ions are very small particles and that ionic size differs from atomic size depending on charge (cations smaller, anions larger).

concepts.name: Examination of a model of the NaCl crystal
concepts.explanation: Practical activity using a physical or virtual model to observe and infer the repeating 3D lattice and ion arrangement in sodium chloride.

concepts.name: Mandatory experiment: Ionic bonding
concepts.explanation: Required practical work focused on ionic bonding concepts (e.g., lattice model observation and linking structure to properties).

concepts.name: Covalent bonding as sharing of electron pairs
concepts.explanation: A covalent bond forms when two atoms share one or more pairs of electrons to achieve a more stable electron arrangement.

concepts.name: Sigma (σ) bond
concepts.explanation: A covalent bond formed by end-to-end orbital overlap with electron density concentrated along the internuclear axis.

concepts.name: Pi (π) bond
concepts.explanation: A covalent bond formed by sideways orbital overlap with electron density above and below the internuclear axis, occurring in addition to a sigma bond in double/triple bonds.

concepts.name: Dot-and-cross diagram for covalent bonding
concepts.explanation: A representation method showing shared and unshared (lone) electrons using different symbols to indicate electrons from different atoms in a covalent bond.

concepts.name: Electron pair repulsion theory (VSEPR) for ABn molecules (up to 4 electron pairs)
concepts.explanation: Use electron pair repulsion to predict the shapes and approximate bond angles of simple ABn molecules with up to four electron pairs around the central atom (excluding cases involving pi bonds).

concepts.name: Molecular shape and bond angle relationships (simple molecules)
concepts.explanation: Recognize common shapes of simple molecules and relate these shapes to characteristic bond angles implied by electron pair geometry.

concepts.name: Symmetry and molecular polarity
concepts.explanation: Determine whether a molecule is polar or nonpolar by considering molecular symmetry and the presence of polar bonds (without requiring dipole moment calculations).

concepts.name: Intramolecular bonding vs intermolecular forces
concepts.explanation: Distinguish bonding within molecules (intramolecular covalent/ionic bonding) from forces between molecules (intermolecular forces).

concepts.name: van der Waals intermolecular forces
concepts.explanation: Identify van der Waals (London dispersion) forces as weak intermolecular attractions present between molecules, especially important in nonpolar substances.

concepts.name: Dipole-dipole intermolecular forces
concepts.explanation: Explain dipole-dipole attractions as intermolecular forces between polar molecules due to permanent dipoles.

concepts.name: Hydrogen bonding
concepts.explanation: Describe hydrogen bonding as a strong intermolecular attraction occurring when H is bonded to highly electronegative atoms (commonly N, O, or F) and interacts with lone pairs on these atoms in neighboring molecules.

concepts.name: Effect of intermolecular forces on boiling point of covalent substances
concepts.explanation: Relate the strength/type of intermolecular forces to boiling point trends in covalent molecular substances (stronger intermolecular forces generally give higher boiling points).

concepts.name: Electronegativity (definition and meaning)
concepts.explanation: Define electronegativity as an atom’s tendency to attract shared electrons in a chemical bond.

concepts.name: Periodic trends in electronegativity (down a group and across a period)
concepts.explanation: Explain general trends in electronegativity values: decreasing down a group and increasing across a period (left to right).

concepts.name: Electronegativity difference and bond polarity
concepts.explanation: Use differences in electronegativity between bonded atoms to determine the polarity of a bond (partial charges).

concepts.name: Predicting bond type from electronegativity difference
concepts.explanation: Classify bonds (e.g., nonpolar covalent, polar covalent, ionic) using electronegativity difference as a predictive guideline.

concepts.name: Oxidation state and oxidation number (definitions)
concepts.explanation: Define oxidation state/oxidation number as the assigned charge an atom would have if bonding electrons were assigned to the more electronegative atom, used for tracking redox changes.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Rules for assigning oxidation numbers (excluding peroxides except hydrogen peroxide)
concepts.explanation: Apply standard rules to assign oxidation numbers in compounds and ions, with peroxide rules generally excluded except for hydrogen peroxide.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Oxidation and reduction in terms of oxidation numbers
concepts.explanation: Identify oxidation as an increase and reduction as a decrease in oxidation number, and use this to determine redox changes in reactions.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Calculating oxidation numbers in transition metal compounds
concepts.explanation: Determine oxidation numbers of transition metals in their compounds using overall charge balance and oxidation number rules.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Oxidation numbers in nomenclature of transition metal compounds
concepts.explanation: Use oxidation numbers to name transition metal compounds (e.g., including the metal oxidation state in the name).

concepts.name: Calculating oxidation numbers of non-transition elements
concepts.explanation: Compute oxidation numbers for other elements in compounds and ions using oxidation number rules and charge balance.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Bleaches as oxidising or reducing agents (examples: NaOCl, SO2)
concepts.explanation: Recognize common bleaching agents and classify them as oxidising agents (e.g., sodium hypochlorite) or reducing agents (e.g., sulfur dioxide) in redox chemistry contexts.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Qualitative test for chloride ions in aqueous solution
concepts.explanation: Carry out and interpret a standard qualitative analysis test to identify chloride ions in aqueous solution.

concepts.name: Qualitative test for carbonate ions in aqueous solution
concepts.explanation: Carry out and interpret a standard qualitative analysis test to identify carbonate ions in aqueous solution.

concepts.name: Qualitative test for nitrate ions in aqueous solution
concepts.explanation: Carry out and interpret a standard qualitative analysis test to identify nitrate ions in aqueous solution.

concepts.name: Qualitative test for sulfate ions in aqueous solution
concepts.explanation: Carry out and interpret a standard qualitative analysis test to identify sulfate ions in aqueous solution.

concepts.name: Qualitative test for phosphate ions in aqueous solution
concepts.explanation: Carry out and interpret a standard qualitative analysis test to identify phosphate ions in aqueous solution.

concepts.name: Qualitative test for sulfite ions in aqueous solution
concepts.explanation: Carry out and interpret a standard qualitative analysis test to identify sulfite ions in aqueous solution.
