concepts.name: Qualitative test for hydrogencarbonate ions in aqueous solution
concepts.explanation: Carry out and interpret a standard qualitative analysis test to identify hydrogencarbonate (bicarbonate) ions in aqueous solution.
concepts.broader_concept: Tests for anions in aqueous solutions

concepts.name: Mole concept
concepts.explanation: The mole as the SI unit for amount of substance, linking macroscopic quantities to number of particles.

concepts.name: Converting between moles, mass, gas volume, and particles
concepts.explanation: Procedures for converting moles to grams, litres, and number of particles and vice versa using molar mass, molar volume, and Avogadro constant.

concepts.name: Converting moles to number of atoms in a molecular species
concepts.explanation: Determining total atoms of a specified element present from moles of molecules and formula subscripts.

concepts.name: Chemical equations
concepts.explanation: Symbolic representations of chemical reactions showing reactants, products, and stoichiometric relationships.

concepts.name: Stoichiometric calculations from balanced equations
concepts.explanation: Using mole ratios from a balanced equation to calculate required or produced amounts (mass or volume).

concepts.name: Limiting reactant and excess reactant calculations
concepts.explanation: Determining which reactant limits product formation and calculating remaining excess reactant.

concepts.name: Percentage yield
concepts.explanation: Comparison of actual yield to theoretical yield expressed as a percentage.

concepts.name: Calculating empirical formula from percentage composition
concepts.explanation: Procedure converting percent-by-mass data to mole ratios and simplifying to obtain the empirical formula.

concepts.name: Calculating empirical formula from masses of reactants and products
concepts.explanation: Deriving an empirical formula using measured masses to determine element amounts and ratios.

concepts.name: Calculating molecular formula from empirical formula and Mr
concepts.explanation: Finding the integer multiple of an empirical formula using the compound’s relative molecular mass.

concepts.name: Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes
concepts.explanation: Reacting gas volumes (at same T and P) are in simple whole-number ratios consistent with the balanced equation.

concepts.name: Avogadro's law
concepts.explanation: Equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules (V ∝ n).

concepts.name: Ideal gas equation (PV = nRT)
concepts.explanation: Equation of state relating pressure, volume, amount (moles), and absolute temperature for an ideal gas.

concepts.name: Correcting gas volumes to s.t.p.
concepts.explanation: Using gas-law relationships to convert measured gas volume at given conditions to the volume at s.t.p.

concepts.name: Kinetic theory of gases (assumptions of ideal gases)
concepts.explanation: Particle model assumptions explaining ideal gas behavior (random motion, negligible volume, elastic collisions, no intermolecular forces).

concepts.name: Deviation from ideal gas behavior
concepts.explanation: Real gases differ from ideal predictions due to intermolecular forces and finite molecular volume (qualitative reasons).

concepts.name: Diffusion in gases and liquids
concepts.explanation: Spontaneous mixing due to random particle motion, illustrated by examples such as NH3/HCl or ink in water.

concepts.name: Balancing redox equations (ionic equations)
concepts.explanation: Balancing oxidation-reduction reactions using ionic equations while ignoring spectator ions.

concepts.name: Determination of relative molecular mass using a mass spectrometer (simple)
concepts.explanation: Using mass spectrometry (without detailed spectral interpretation) to determine relative molecular mass (Mr).

concepts.name: Determination of relative molecular mass of a volatile liquid
concepts.explanation: Experimental method to determine Mr of a volatile liquid using apparatus such as a conical flask or gas syringe.

concepts.name: Boyle’s air pump demonstration
concepts.explanation: Using an air pump to demonstrate the pressure–volume relationship for gases (Boyle’s law).

concepts.name: Solution concentration units (g L−1 and percentage forms)
concepts.explanation: Expressing concentration as grams per litre and as % (w/v), % (v/v), and % (w/w).

concepts.name: Converting between molarity and g L−1
concepts.explanation: Using molar mass to convert concentration units between mol L−1 and g L−1.

concepts.name: Calculating moles from molarity and volume
concepts.explanation: Using n = cV (with V in litres) to determine amount of solute from solution concentration and volume.

concepts.name: Dilution calculations
concepts.explanation: Determining how concentration changes when a solution is diluted (e.g., using c1V1 = c2V2).

concepts.name: Acids, bases and salts (definitions)
concepts.explanation: Core classification of substances as acids, bases, or salts in aqueous chemistry.

concepts.name: Arrhenius theory of acids and bases (aqueous)
concepts.explanation: Acids produce H+ (or H3O+) in water and bases produce OH− in water.

concepts.name: Brønsted-Lowry theory of acids and bases (aqueous)
concepts.explanation: Acids donate protons (H+) and bases accept protons in aqueous solutions.

concepts.name: Conjugate acid-base pairs
concepts.explanation: Pairs of species differing by one proton, linked by acid-base reactions.

concepts.name: Volumetric analysis
concepts.explanation: Quantitative analysis method in which concentration or amount of a substance is determined by measuring volumes of reacting solutions, typically using titration.

concepts.name: Titrimetric (titration) procedure
concepts.explanation: Standard sequence of steps for carrying out a titration accurately (rinsing apparatus, filling burette, pipetting aliquot, adding indicator, titrating to endpoint, repeating for concordant titres).

concepts.name: Apparatus used in volumetric analysis
concepts.explanation: Use and purpose of volumetric glassware (burette, pipette, volumetric flask, conical flask) for accurate measurement and delivery of solutions.

concepts.name: Standard solution preparation
concepts.explanation: Preparing a solution of accurately known concentration by weighing a primary standard and making up to a precise volume in a volumetric flask.

concepts.name: Primary standard (sodium carbonate as a primary standard)
concepts.explanation: A pure, stable solid used to prepare a standard solution by direct weighing; sodium carbonate is used to make a standard alkali for acid standardisation.

concepts.name: Standardisation of a solution
concepts.explanation: Determining the exact concentration of a solution by titrating it against a standard solution of known concentration.

concepts.name: Redox titration
concepts.explanation: Titration based on oxidation-reduction reactions where electron transfer stoichiometry determines concentration, often using self-indicating or redox indicators.

concepts.name: Formula method for volumetric calculations
concepts.explanation: Solving titration problems using a standard relationship (e.g., n = C×V with stoichiometric ratios from the balanced equation) in a structured formula approach.

concepts.name: First-principles volumetric calculations
concepts.explanation: Solving titration problems by reasoning from moles, concentration, volume, and stoichiometric ratios without relying on a memorised formula.

concepts.name: Using balanced equations in volumetric problems
concepts.explanation: Applying coefficients from a balanced chemical equation to relate reacting moles in titration calculations.

concepts.name: Determination of relative molecular mass from titration data
concepts.explanation: Calculating the relative molecular mass of a compound by using titration-derived moles and measured mass of sample.

concepts.name: Water of crystallisation determination by titration
concepts.explanation: Finding the number of moles of water of crystallisation in a hydrated salt by titrating a known mass and comparing with anhydrous content via stoichiometry.

concepts.name: Preparation of a standard sodium carbonate solution (experiment)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory preparation of a standard Na2CO3 solution by accurate weighing, dissolving, and making up to volume for use in titrations.

concepts.name: Standardisation of hydrochloric acid using sodium carbonate (experiment)
concepts.explanation: Determining the concentration of HCl by titrating it against a standard Na2CO3 solution and using stoichiometry to calculate acid concentration.

concepts.name: Determination of ethanoic acid concentration in vinegar (experiment)
concepts.explanation: Acid-base titration of vinegar to calculate ethanoic acid concentration, typically via neutralisation with a standard alkali.

concepts.name: Determination of water of crystallisation in hydrated sodium carbonate (experiment)
concepts.explanation: Using titration data from a hydrated Na2CO3 sample to determine the value of x in Na2CO3·xH2O.

concepts.name: Potassium manganate(VII) vs ammonium iron(II) sulfate titration
concepts.explanation: Redox titration where KMnO4 oxidises Fe2+ (from Mohr's salt) to Fe3+, used to determine concentration using redox stoichiometry.

concepts.name: Determination of iron content in an iron tablet (experiment)
concepts.explanation: Quantifying iron in a tablet by converting iron to a titratable form and using redox titration data to calculate mass of iron present.

concepts.name: Iodine-thiosulfate titration (iodometry)
concepts.explanation: Redox titration in which iodine is titrated with sodium thiosulfate to determine iodine (or an oxidant that generates iodine) via stoichiometry.

concepts.name: Determination of hypochlorite concentration in bleach (% w/v) (experiment)
concepts.explanation: Determining the percentage mass per volume of hypochlorite in bleach, commonly via iodometric titration and calculation of % (w/v).

concepts.name: Calculations based on titration experimental data
concepts.explanation: Processing titre values and sample data to compute concentrations, masses, or percentages, including use of concordant titres and stoichiometric relationships.

concepts.name: Law of conservation of energy (thermochemistry context)
concepts.explanation: Energy cannot be created or destroyed; heat released by a system is gained by the surroundings and vice versa, underpinning calorimetry and Hess’s law.

concepts.name: Hess’s law
concepts.explanation: The enthalpy change for an overall reaction equals the sum of enthalpy changes for any set of steps that add to the same overall equation.

concepts.name: Heat of formation (standard enthalpy of formation)
concepts.explanation: The enthalpy change when 1 mole of a compound forms from its elements in their standard states under standard conditions.

concepts.name: Calculating heat of reaction using heats of formation
concepts.explanation: Using ΔHreaction = ΣΔHf(products) − ΣΔHf(reactants) to obtain a reaction enthalpy from tabulated formation enthalpies.

concepts.name: Calculating an unknown heat of formation using Hess’s law
concepts.explanation: Rearranging formation enthalpies and a known reaction enthalpy to solve for an unknown ΔHf value.

concepts.name: Bond energy (bond enthalpy) concept
concepts.explanation: The energy required to break a covalent bond in the gas phase; used qualitatively to relate bond breaking/forming to reaction enthalpy.

concepts.name: Illustrative bond energy calculation for methane C–H bonds
concepts.explanation: Using measured enthalpy data to estimate an average C–H bond energy in methane as an illustrative example (not general bond-energy problem solving).

concepts.name: Comparing heats of combustion of fuels
concepts.explanation: Interpreting and comparing fuel energy outputs based on their heats of combustion to assess relative energy content.

concepts.name: Calorific value (kilogram calorific value)
concepts.explanation: Energy released per unit mass of fuel during complete combustion (e.g., kJ kg−1), used to compare fuels and food energy content.

concepts.name: Mandatory experiment: heat of reaction of HCl with NaOH
concepts.explanation: Determining the enthalpy change of neutralization by mixing hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide and measuring temperature change in a calorimetry setup.

concepts.name: Complete combustion of hydrocarbons
concepts.explanation: Reaction of a hydrocarbon with excess oxygen to produce carbon dioxide and water, releasing heat (typically exothermic).

concepts.name: Hydrocarbon sources: coal, natural gas, petroleum
concepts.explanation: Identifying coal, natural gas and crude oil as major natural sources from which hydrocarbons are obtained.

concepts.name: Methane from anaerobic decomposition
concepts.explanation: Production of methane during decomposition of animal waste and vegetation in low-oxygen conditions (biogas formation).

concepts.name: Hazards of methane accumulation
concepts.explanation: Safety risks from methane production and buildup in slurry pits, coal mines and refuse dumps, including flammability and explosion hazards.

concepts.name: Methane as a greenhouse gas contributor
concepts.explanation: Methane’s role in enhancing the greenhouse effect due to its infrared absorption, contributing to climate warming.

concepts.name: Systematic naming of alkanes up to C5
concepts.explanation: Applying IUPAC rules to name straight-chain and branched alkanes containing up to five carbon atoms.

concepts.name: Structural formulas of alkanes up to C5
concepts.explanation: Representing alkanes (up to C5) using structural formulas that show carbon connectivity and hydrogen placement.

concepts.name: Structural isomerism in alkanes up to C5
concepts.explanation: Different connectivity arrangements (isomers) for alkanes with the same molecular formula, considered up to five carbons.

concepts.name: Recognising structures of higher alkanes and cycloalkanes (specified examples)
concepts.explanation: Identifying and drawing structures (not isomers) of hexane, heptane, octane, cyclohexane and 2,2,4-trimethylpentane (iso-octane).

concepts.name: Systematic naming of alkenes up to C4
concepts.explanation: Applying IUPAC rules to name alkenes containing up to four carbon atoms, including position of the double bond.

concepts.name: Structural formulas of alkenes up to C4
concepts.explanation: Representing alkenes (up to C4) using structural formulas showing carbon–carbon double bonds.

concepts.name: Structural isomerism in alkenes up to C4
concepts.explanation: Different connectivity/position isomers for alkenes with the same molecular formula, considered up to four carbons.

concepts.name: Ethyne as the representative alkyne
concepts.explanation: Limiting alkyne study to ethyne (acetylene) as the key example of a triple-bond hydrocarbon.

concepts.name: Solubility of hydrocarbons in water vs non-polar solvents (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: Hydrocarbons are generally insoluble in water but soluble in non-polar solvents; assessed qualitatively.

concepts.name: Physical state trends in hydrocarbons (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: Recognising that hydrocarbon physical state varies with molecular size/structure (e.g., smaller are gases, larger are liquids/solids).

concepts.name: Using molecular models to represent hydrocarbon structures
concepts.explanation: Employing ball-and-stick or similar models to visualise shapes, bonding and connectivity in hydrocarbons.

concepts.name: Aromatic structure of benzene
concepts.explanation: Benzene as an aromatic compound with a ring structure and delocalised bonding representation (structure-level understanding).

concepts.name: Structures of methylbenzene and ethylbenzene
concepts.explanation: Recognising methylbenzene (toluene) and ethylbenzene as substituted benzene (aromatic) structures.

concepts.name: Major crude oil fractions (refinery gas to residue)
concepts.explanation: Identifying refinery gas, light gasoline, naphtha, kerosene, gas oil and residue as main fractions from crude oil.

concepts.name: Uses of crude oil fractions
concepts.explanation: Matching each refinery fraction (e.g., kerosene, gas oil) to typical applications such as fuels and feedstocks.

concepts.name: Composition of natural gas and LPG
concepts.explanation: Natural gas as mainly methane with other light hydrocarbons; LPG as mainly propane and butane (composition-level understanding).

concepts.name: Petrol composition (mixture of hydrocarbons)
concepts.explanation: Understanding petrol (gasoline) as a blend of hydrocarbons tailored for engine performance.

concepts.name: Auto-ignition in internal combustion engines
concepts.explanation: Premature ignition of the fuel–air mixture due to compression/heat, linked to engine knocking.

concepts.name: Octane number as a measure of knocking tendency
concepts.explanation: A fuel rating indicating resistance to knocking/auto-ignition; higher octane means greater resistance.

concepts.name: Effect of chain length on octane number (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: Longer straight-chain hydrocarbons generally have lower octane numbers (more knocking) than shorter/branched analogues.

concepts.name: Effect of branching on octane number (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: More highly branched hydrocarbons generally have higher octane numbers (less knocking) than straight-chain isomers.

concepts.name: Effect of cyclic structure on octane number (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: Cyclic hydrocarbons typically have higher octane numbers than corresponding straight-chain structures (qualitative comparison).

concepts.name: Lead additives in petrol (antiknock)
concepts.explanation: Historically using lead compounds to improve octane number and reduce knocking, with associated environmental/health concerns.

concepts.name: Isomerisation to improve octane number
concepts.explanation: Refinery process converting straight-chain hydrocarbons into branched isomers to raise octane rating.

concepts.name: Dehydrocyclisation to improve octane number
concepts.explanation: Refinery process forming cyclic/aromatic structures (with loss of hydrogen) from alkanes to increase octane number.

concepts.name: Catalytic cracking to improve petrol yield and octane
concepts.explanation: Breaking larger hydrocarbons into smaller alkanes and alkenes using a catalyst to increase gasoline production and typically improve octane.

concepts.name: Oxygenates to increase octane number (MTBE example)
concepts.explanation: Adding oxygen-containing compounds (e.g., methyl tert-butyl ether) to petrol to raise octane and reduce certain emissions.

concepts.name: Preparation of ethyne
concepts.explanation: Laboratory preparation of ethyne (acetylene) as a fuel and unsaturated hydrocarbon (method-level understanding as per syllabus experiment).

concepts.name: Combustion of ethyne
concepts.explanation: Burning ethyne in oxygen/air to produce carbon dioxide and water with high heat output; basis for oxyacetylene applications.

concepts.name: Mandatory experiment: preparation and properties of ethyne
concepts.explanation: Carrying out ethyne preparation and investigating combustion and tests for unsaturation using bromine water and acidified KMnO4.

concepts.name: Oxyacetylene welding and cutting (chemical basis)
concepts.explanation: Using the high-temperature combustion of ethyne in oxygen to generate a flame suitable for welding and cutting metals.

concepts.name: Hydrogen production by steam reforming of natural gas (simple treatment)
concepts.explanation: Producing hydrogen from methane and steam (industrial process overview), yielding hydrogen and carbon-containing products.

concepts.name: Hydrogen as a potential fuel (industrial context)
concepts.explanation: Considering hydrogen’s use as a fuel and its industrial relevance, including production routes and energy considerations at a qualitative level.

concepts.name: Average rate of reaction
concepts.explanation: Rate calculated over a finite time interval as total change in concentration (or amount) divided by the time taken.

concepts.name: Instantaneous rate of reaction
concepts.explanation: Rate at a specific moment in time, obtained from the slope of the tangent to a concentration–time (or similar) graph at that point.

concepts.name: Reaction rate graph (rate vs time or concentration vs time) interpretation
concepts.explanation: Reading and interpreting reaction progress graphs to determine how reaction rate changes with time and to compare rates under different conditions.

concepts.name: Determining instantaneous rate from a graph
concepts.explanation: Procedure for calculating instantaneous rate by drawing a tangent at a chosen point on the curve and finding its gradient (with correct units and sign).

concepts.name: Mandatory experiment: plotting reaction rate graphs
concepts.explanation: Laboratory investigation in which reaction progress data are collected and plotted to produce reaction rate graphs for simple interpretation.

concepts.name: Activation energy
concepts.explanation: Minimum energy barrier that reacting particles must overcome for a reaction to occur.

concepts.name: Reaction profile (energy) diagrams
concepts.explanation: Graphical representation of energy changes during a reaction showing reactants, products, and activation energy.

concepts.name: Influence of temperature on activation energy barrier crossing
concepts.explanation: Temperature increases the fraction of particles with energy equal to or greater than activation energy, increasing rate without changing Ea for an uncatalysed pathway.

concepts.name: Effect of catalysts on activation energy
concepts.explanation: Catalysts lower the activation energy by providing an alternative reaction pathway, increasing rate without being consumed.

concepts.name: Surface adsorption theory of catalysis
concepts.explanation: Model of heterogeneous catalysis where reactant molecules adsorb onto a catalyst surface, increasing effective collision frequency and enabling reaction.

concepts.name: Intermediate formation theory of catalysis
concepts.explanation: Catalysis model where a temporary intermediate forms between catalyst and reactants, then breaks down to products while regenerating the catalyst.

concepts.name: Demonstration: effect of particle size on reaction rate
concepts.explanation: Practical demonstration comparing reaction rates using different particle sizes to show increased surface area increases rate.

concepts.name: Demonstration: effect of catalysts on reaction rate
concepts.explanation: Practical demonstration showing a catalyst increases reaction rate compared with an uncatalysed reaction under similar conditions.

concepts.name: Mandatory experiment 6.1: rate of oxygen production from hydrogen peroxide using manganese dioxide
concepts.explanation: Procedure to monitor oxygen evolution from decomposition of hydrogen peroxide with MnO2 as a catalyst to study rate over time.
concepts.broader_concept: Measuring reaction rates using gas production

concepts.name: Mandatory experiment 6.2: effect of concentration and temperature on sodium thiosulfate–hydrochloric acid reaction rate
concepts.explanation: Using the sodium thiosulfate and hydrochloric acid reaction (often timed by disappearance of a mark due to sulfur formation) to study how concentration and temperature change rate.
concepts.broader_concept: Experimental investigation of concentration and temperature effects

concepts.name: Demonstration: oxidation of methanol catalysed by hot platinum or nichrome
concepts.explanation: Demonstration of catalytic oxidation of methanol using a heated metal catalyst (platinum or nichrome) to illustrate catalysis in oxidation reactions.

concepts.name: Demonstration: oxidation of potassium sodium tartrate by hydrogen peroxide catalysed by cobalt(II) salts
concepts.explanation: Demonstration showing cobalt(II) salts catalyse the oxidation of potassium sodium tartrate by hydrogen peroxide, illustrating transition-metal catalysis.

concepts.name: Dust explosions
concepts.explanation: Rapid combustion of fine particulate solids due to very high surface area and effective mixing with oxygen, causing explosive rate increases.
concepts.broader_concept: Surface area effects and combustion hazards

concepts.name: Enzymes as biological catalysts
concepts.explanation: Enzymes are catalysts produced by living cells that increase reaction rates under mild conditions and are not consumed in the reaction.

concepts.name: Examples of enzymes as catalysts
concepts.explanation: Using specific named enzyme examples to illustrate enzyme-catalysed reactions and their conditions (two examples required by syllabus).

concepts.name: Catalytic converters: nature of catalysts
concepts.explanation: Composition and role of catalysts in catalytic converters (typically noble metals on supports) enabling faster conversion of pollutants.

concepts.name: Catalytic converters: reactions catalysed
concepts.explanation: Key conversion reactions in exhaust systems (e.g., oxidation of CO and hydrocarbons; reduction of nitrogen oxides) enabled by catalysts.

concepts.name: Catalytic converters: environmental benefits
concepts.explanation: How catalytic converters reduce harmful emissions (CO, unburnt hydrocarbons, NOx), improving air quality.
concepts.broader_concept: Chemistry and environmental impact of catalysis

concepts.name: Catalyst poisons
concepts.explanation: Substances that reduce catalyst activity by binding strongly to active sites or otherwise deactivating the catalyst (e.g., fouling/poisoning).

concepts.name: Tetrahedral geometry of saturated carbon (sp3)
concepts.explanation: Carbon in saturated organic compounds forms four single bonds arranged tetrahedrally.
concepts.broader_concept: Carbon bonding and molecular geometry in organic chemistry

concepts.name: Planar carbon in alkenes (C=C, sp2)
concepts.explanation: Alkenes contain a carbon–carbon double bond with trigonal planar arrangement around the double-bonded carbons.
concepts.broader_concept: Carbon bonding and molecular geometry in organic chemistry

concepts.name: Saturated organic compounds (alkanes)
concepts.explanation: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons containing only C–C single bonds and C–H bonds.

concepts.name: Unsaturated organic compounds (alkenes)
concepts.explanation: Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing at least one C=C double bond.

concepts.name: Structural formulas for organic molecules
concepts.explanation: Using structural formulas to represent connectivity and bond types in organic compounds for naming and reactions.

concepts.name: Writing balanced organic reaction equations using structural formulas
concepts.explanation: Balancing addition, substitution and polymerisation reaction equations while showing organic structures.

concepts.name: Nomenclature of alkanes up to C4
concepts.explanation: Naming straight-chain alkanes from methane to butane using standard nomenclature.

concepts.name: Nomenclature of alkenes up to C4
concepts.explanation: Naming alkenes up to four carbons, including position of the C=C double bond (where relevant).

concepts.name: Chloroalkanes: structure and nomenclature up to C4
concepts.explanation: Recognising and naming haloalkanes containing chlorine substituents for chains up to four carbons.

concepts.name: Alcohols (primary and secondary): structure and nomenclature up to C4
concepts.explanation: Identifying the –OH functional group, distinguishing primary vs secondary alcohols, and naming alcohols up to four carbons.

concepts.name: Carbonyl group polarity (C=O)
concepts.explanation: The C=O double bond is polar due to electronegativity difference, influencing physical properties and reactivity.

concepts.name: Aldehydes: structure and nomenclature up to C4
concepts.explanation: Identifying aldehydes (terminal carbonyl, –CHO) and naming aldehydes up to four carbons (e.g., ethanal).

concepts.name: Ketones: structure and nomenclature up to C4
concepts.explanation: Identifying ketones (internal carbonyl) and naming ketones up to four carbons (e.g., propanone).

concepts.name: Carboxylic acids: structure and nomenclature up to C4
concepts.explanation: Identifying the –COOH functional group and naming carboxylic acids up to four carbons (e.g., ethanoic acid).

concepts.name: Esters: structural formulas and nomenclature up to C4
concepts.explanation: Recognising ester functional group (–COO–), writing structural formulas, and naming simple esters up to C4 (e.g., ethyl ethanoate).

concepts.name: Physical state trends in small organic molecules
concepts.explanation: Relating molecular size and intermolecular forces to whether small organic compounds are gases, liquids, or solids (qualitative).

concepts.name: Solubility comparison experiment: methanol vs butan-1-ol in water and cyclohexane
concepts.explanation: Procedure-based comparison showing how increasing hydrocarbon chain length reduces water solubility and increases solubility in non-polar solvents.
concepts.broader_concept: Experimental investigation of solubility and polarity

concepts.name: Solubility test: propanone in water vs cyclohexane
concepts.explanation: Comparing solubility of a ketone in polar and non-polar solvents to infer effects of the carbonyl group.
concepts.broader_concept: Experimental investigation of solubility and polarity

concepts.name: Mandatory experiment: solubility of ethyl ethanoate in water vs cyclohexane
concepts.explanation: Investigating ester solubility in polar and non-polar solvents to relate ester polarity to observed solubility.
concepts.broader_concept: Experimental investigation of solubility and polarity

concepts.name: Addition reactions of alkenes
concepts.explanation: Alkenes undergo addition across the C=C bond to form more saturated products.

concepts.name: Hydrogenation of alkenes (addition of H2)
concepts.explanation: Addition of hydrogen across a C=C bond to form an alkane (e.g., ethene to ethane).

concepts.name: Halogen addition to alkenes (Cl2 and Br2)
concepts.explanation: Addition of chlorine or bromine across the C=C bond to form dihaloalkanes.

concepts.name: Hydrohalogenation of alkenes (addition of HCl)
concepts.explanation: Addition of hydrogen chloride across a C=C bond to form a chloroalkane (haloalkane).

concepts.name: Ionic addition mechanism to ethene (electrophilic addition)
concepts.explanation: Mechanistic description of addition of HCl, Br2, or Cl2 to ethene via ionic intermediates.

concepts.name: Evidence for ionic addition: ethene + bromine water with sodium chloride gives mixed products
concepts.explanation: Product mixture (2-bromoethanol, 1-bromo-2-chloroethane, 1,2-dibromoethane) supports an ionic addition pathway with competing nucleophiles.

concepts.name: Substitution reactions of alkanes (halogenation)
concepts.explanation: Alkanes undergo substitution where a hydrogen atom is replaced by a halogen atom (e.g., chlorination).

concepts.name: Free radical substitution mechanism (monochlorination of methane and ethane)
concepts.explanation: Chain mechanism (initiation, propagation, termination) describing monochlorination of methane and ethane.

concepts.name: Evidence for free radical substitution: UV light initiates chain reaction
concepts.explanation: Ultraviolet light triggers formation of radicals that sustain a chain process during alkane chlorination.

concepts.name: Evidence for free radical substitution: formation of ethane and butane traces
concepts.explanation: Trace ethane (from methane chlorination) and butane (from ethane chlorination) indicate radical coupling termination steps.

concepts.name: Evidence for free radical substitution: reactions accelerated by radical initiators (e.g., tetraethyllead)
concepts.explanation: Adding a radical source speeds up chlorination, supporting a free radical chain mechanism.

concepts.name: Benzene ring representation with a circle (delocalised bonding)
concepts.explanation: The circle in benzene depicts identical intermediate bonds due to delocalised electrons, rather than alternating single/double bonds.

concepts.name: Sigma and pi bonding in benzene
concepts.explanation: Benzene has a sigma framework and a delocalised pi system contributing to equalised bond character.

concepts.name: Unreactivity of benzene toward addition reactions compared with ethene
concepts.explanation: Benzene resists addition reactions relative to alkenes due to stabilisation associated with aromatic bonding.

concepts.name: Esterification (formation of esters)
concepts.explanation: Reaction in which an alcohol reacts with a carboxylic acid to form an ester (and water), typically acid-catalysed.

concepts.name: Base hydrolysis of esters (saponification)
concepts.explanation: Alkaline hydrolysis of an ester to produce an alcohol and a carboxylate salt (often leading to soap formation for fatty acid esters).

concepts.name: Dehydration of alcohols (elimination)
concepts.explanation: Elimination reaction where an alcohol loses water to form an alkene under suitable conditions (acid/heat).

concepts.name: Oxidation of alcohols to aldehydes
concepts.explanation: Oxidation of (typically primary) alcohols using oxidising agents such as KMnO4 or Na2Cr2O7 to form aldehydes; represented using half-equations at this level.

concepts.name: Oxidation of alcohols to carboxylic acids
concepts.explanation: Further oxidation of (primary) alcohols using KMnO4 or Na2Cr2O7 to form carboxylic acids; half-equations used for redox representation.

concepts.name: Resistance of ketones to oxidation
concepts.explanation: Ketones are not easily oxidised under typical school-level oxidising conditions compared with aldehydes.

concepts.name: Reduction of carbonyl compounds using H2/Ni
concepts.explanation: Hydrogenation of aldehydes/ketones using hydrogen gas and a nickel catalyst to produce alcohols.

concepts.name: Combustion reactions of organic compounds
concepts.explanation: Oxidation (burning) of organic compounds in oxygen, typically producing CO2 and H2O; presented as a common reaction type for organics.

concepts.name: Reaction of alcohols with sodium
concepts.explanation: Alcohols react with sodium metal to form sodium alkoxides and hydrogen gas, demonstrating weak acidity of alcohols.

concepts.name: Acidic nature of the carboxylic acid functional group
concepts.explanation: Carboxylic acids donate H+ from the –COOH group, showing typical acid reactions and greater acidity than alcohols.

concepts.name: Reaction of carboxylic acids with magnesium
concepts.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with magnesium metal to form a magnesium carboxylate salt and hydrogen gas.

concepts.name: Neutralisation of carboxylic acids with sodium hydroxide
concepts.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with NaOH to form sodium carboxylate salts and water.

concepts.name: Reaction of carboxylic acids with sodium carbonate
concepts.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with Na2CO3 to form sodium carboxylate salts, water, and carbon dioxide gas.

concepts.name: Principles of organic synthesis (bond breaking and bond forming)
concepts.explanation: Organic synthesis is framed as a sequence of reactions involving breaking bonds and forming new bonds to build target molecules.

concepts.name: Synthesis of PVC from ethene (polymerisation route)
concepts.explanation: Preparation of PVC starting from ethene via a specified synthetic route (including required structures), as an example of industrial organic synthesis.

concepts.name: Constructing organic reaction schemes (up to three conversions)
concepts.explanation: Planning multistep synthesis by linking familiar organic reactions into a reaction pathway of up to three steps.

concepts.name: Percentage yield calculation in organic preparations
concepts.explanation: Calculation of percentage yield from actual yield and theoretical yield using a balanced chemical equation (provided).

concepts.name: Soap manufacture (from esters/fats)
concepts.explanation: Production of soap via base hydrolysis of esters (e.g., triglycerides) to form carboxylate salts; structures of reactants and products required.
concepts.broader_concept: Industrial and applied organic chemistry: saponification

concepts.name: Petrochemical industry: synthetic products
concepts.explanation: Awareness of the range and scope of petrochemicals through examples of synthetic products derived from petroleum feedstocks.

concepts.name: Chromatography (mobile phase and stationary phase)
concepts.explanation: Separation technique where a mixture is carried by a mobile phase past a selectively adsorbent stationary phase, leading to separation due to differing affinities.

concepts.name: Thin-layer chromatography (TLC) for separating dyes from fibres
concepts.explanation: Application of TLC to separate dye components extracted from fibres, including use in forensic analysis.

concepts.name: Solvent extraction
concepts.explanation: Separation method using differential solubility of substances between immiscible solvents to isolate desired organic compounds.

concepts.name: Steam distillation
concepts.explanation: Technique to isolate temperature-sensitive or high-boiling organic compounds by co-distillation with steam.

concepts.name: Gas chromatography (GC) as a separation technique
concepts.explanation: Instrumental method separating volatile components as they partition between a gas mobile phase and a stationary phase in a column.

concepts.name: High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) as a separation technique
concepts.explanation: Instrumental chromatographic method using high pressure to pass a liquid mobile phase through a column to separate components by interaction with the stationary phase.

concepts.name: Mass spectrometry (MS) for analysis
concepts.explanation: Instrumental analytical method that separates ions by mass-to-charge ratio to provide information useful for identifying substances.

concepts.name: Infrared (IR) absorption spectrometry as fingerprinting
concepts.explanation: Analytical technique where absorption of infrared radiation produces a characteristic spectrum used to identify compounds (fingerprinting; detailed vibration theory not required).

concepts.name: Ultraviolet (UV) absorption spectrometry for quantitative analysis
concepts.explanation: Quantitative technique based on absorption of ultraviolet light to determine concentration of analytes (detailed spectral interpretation not required).

concepts.name: Organic natural products (examples and usefulness)
concepts.explanation: Awareness of the scope of organic natural product chemistry through examples of useful naturally occurring organic compounds (structures not required).

concepts.name: Recrystallisation (purification technique)
concepts.explanation: Purification of a solid by dissolving in a hot solvent and reforming crystals on cooling, leaving impurities in solution.

concepts.name: Melting point determination (organic solid identification)
concepts.explanation: Measuring the melting point of a purified solid (e.g., benzoic acid) to assess purity and help identify the compound.

concepts.name: Ethene preparation (laboratory)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory preparation of ethene as an alkene for subsequent testing of its properties.

concepts.name: Ethanal preparation (laboratory)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory preparation of ethanal (an aldehyde) for testing characteristic aldehyde reactions.

concepts.name: Fehling’s test for aldehydes (ethanal)
concepts.explanation: Aldehydes reduce Fehling’s reagent to a brick-red precipitate of Cu2O on warming, distinguishing aldehydes from many ketones.

concepts.name: Tollens’ test (ammoniacal silver nitrate) for aldehydes
concepts.explanation: Aldehydes reduce Tollens’ reagent to metallic silver (silver mirror/black deposit), providing a test for aldehyde functional groups.

concepts.name: Ethanoic acid preparation (laboratory)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory preparation of ethanoic acid for investigation of typical carboxylic acid reactions.

concepts.name: Esterification of ethanoic acid with ethanol
concepts.explanation: Reaction of ethanoic acid with ethanol to form an ester (ethyl ethanoate) and water, typically acid-catalysed.

concepts.name: Trace organic pollutant analysis (water)
concepts.explanation: Analytical measurement and identification of very low concentrations of organic contaminants in water samples.
concepts.broader_concept: Analytical chemistry applications in environmental monitoring

concepts.name: Gas analysis from waste dumps
concepts.explanation: Sampling and analysis of gases emitted from waste dumps to identify and/or quantify gaseous components.
concepts.broader_concept: Analytical chemistry applications in environmental monitoring

concepts.name: Drug testing in athletes (analysis of drug compounds/metabolites)
concepts.explanation: Detection and measurement of drugs or their metabolites in biological samples using analytical methods.
concepts.broader_concept: Analytical chemistry applications in health and forensics

concepts.name: Identification of organic compounds (e.g., plastics, drugs)
concepts.explanation: Using characteristic properties and tests to determine the identity of unknown organic substances such as polymers and pharmaceuticals.

concepts.name: Quantitative determination of organic compounds (e.g., metabolites, pigments)
concepts.explanation: Measuring the amount or concentration of specific organic substances in a sample for analytical or quality-control purposes.

concepts.name: Equilibrium law (law of mass action) for Kc
concepts.explanation: For a reaction at equilibrium, Kc is expressed as the product of equilibrium concentrations of products divided by reactants, each raised to their stoichiometric coefficients.

concepts.name: Calculations using Kc
concepts.explanation: Solving equilibrium problems by substituting equilibrium concentrations into the Kc expression (often using ICE tables) to find unknown concentrations.

concepts.name: Le Chatelier's principle
concepts.explanation: When a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it shifts position to oppose the imposed change and partially counteract the disturbance.

concepts.name: Le Chatelier experiment: cobalt(II) chloride complex equilibrium
concepts.explanation: Demonstrating equilibrium shifts with the system CoCl4^2− + 6H2O ⇌ [Co(H2O)6]^2+ + 4Cl− by changing temperature and chloride/water concentration to observe color changes.

concepts.name: Le Chatelier experiment: dichromate–chromate equilibrium shift
concepts.explanation: Using the equilibrium Cr2O7^2− + H2O ⇌ 2CrO4^2− + 2H+ to show how changing concentration (e.g., adding acid/base) shifts equilibrium with visible color change.

concepts.name: Le Chatelier experiment: iron(III) thiocyanate complex formation
concepts.explanation: Demonstrating concentration effects using Fe3+ + SCN− ⇌ FeSCN2+ where adding/removing ions shifts equilibrium and changes the intensity of the red complex.

concepts.name: Industrial application: Haber process equilibrium control
concepts.explanation: Applying Le Chatelier’s principle to ammonia synthesis by optimizing conditions (pressure, temperature, removal of NH3) to improve yield.

concepts.name: Industrial application: catalytic oxidation of SO2 to SO3 equilibrium control
concepts.explanation: Applying Le Chatelier’s principle to 2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3 by selecting temperature/pressure and removing SO3 to maximize SO3 yield in sulfuric acid manufacture.

concepts.name: Self-ionisation of water
concepts.explanation: Equilibrium process where water molecules produce hydronium and hydroxide ions (2H2O ⇌ H3O+ + OH−), forming the basis of aqueous acidity/basicity.

concepts.name: Ionic product of water (Kw)
concepts.explanation: Equilibrium constant for water self-ionisation, Kw = [H3O+][OH−], used to relate acidity and basicity in aqueous solutions at a given temperature.

concepts.name: Limitations of the pH scale in concentrated solutions
concepts.explanation: Recognition that pH is most useful for dilute aqueous solutions because it is based on concentration/activity assumptions that break down at higher ionic strength.

concepts.name: Universal indicator for pH estimation
concepts.explanation: Use of universal indicator paper/solution to estimate pH by comparing colour to a reference chart.

concepts.name: Calculation of pH for strong acids in dilute aqueous solution
concepts.explanation: Computing pH from [H3O+] assuming complete ionisation for dilute strong acids (without requiring strong acid–strong base mixture calculations).

concepts.name: Calculation of pH for strong bases in dilute aqueous solution
concepts.explanation: Computing pOH from [OH−] assuming complete ionisation for dilute strong bases, then converting to pH using pH + pOH = 14 (at 25°C).

concepts.name: Approximation in weak acid/base pH calculations (non-ionised concentration unchanged)
concepts.explanation: Using the assumption that ionisation is small so the concentration of the non-ionised species is approximately equal to the initial concentration when estimating pH/pOH for weak acids/bases.

concepts.name: pH of weak acids and weak bases
concepts.explanation: Understanding that weak acids/bases partially ionise in water, producing pH values determined by equilibrium rather than complete dissociation.

concepts.name: Acid-base indicators (theory)
concepts.explanation: Indicators are weak acids/bases whose conjugate forms have different colours; colour depends on the position of the indicator equilibrium and solution pH.

concepts.name: Choice of indicator for titrations
concepts.explanation: Selecting an indicator with a transition range that lies within the steep pH change (near the equivalence point) on the titration curve.

concepts.name: Acid-base titration curves
concepts.explanation: Graphs of pH versus volume of titrant added, used to identify equivalence point regions and inform indicator choice.

concepts.name: Temporary hardness of water
concepts.explanation: Hardness caused mainly by dissolved calcium/magnesium hydrogencarbonates, removable by boiling (forms carbonate precipitate and releases CO2).

concepts.name: Permanent hardness of water
concepts.explanation: Hardness caused mainly by calcium/magnesium sulfates or chlorides, not removed by boiling and typically treated by ion exchange or other methods.

concepts.name: Ion-exchange removal of hardness
concepts.explanation: Softening by exchanging Ca2+/Mg2+ ions with Na+ (or H+) ions on a resin, reducing hardness without boiling.

concepts.name: Relative purity of deionised water vs distilled water
concepts.explanation: Comparison that deionised water removes ions effectively but may still contain non-ionic impurities, whereas distillation removes many dissolved substances but not necessarily all volatiles.

concepts.name: Scale deposit testing (kettle deposits)
concepts.explanation: Identifying scale as mainly carbonate deposits (e.g., CaCO3) using simple chemical tests (e.g., reaction with acid producing CO2).

concepts.name: Primary sewage treatment (screening and settlement)
concepts.explanation: Physical removal of large solids and settling of suspended material as the first stage of wastewater treatment.

concepts.name: Eutrophication and nutrient enrichment
concepts.explanation: Process where increased nutrients (nitrates/phosphates) stimulate algal growth, leading to oxygen depletion and ecosystem damage.

concepts.name: Nitrate fertiliser runoff as a water pollutant
concepts.explanation: Uncontrolled use of nitrate fertilisers can lead to leaching/runoff into water bodies, contributing to eutrophication and water-quality issues.

concepts.name: Heavy metal ion pollution in water (Pb2+, Hg2+, Cd2+)
concepts.explanation: Contamination of water by toxic metal ions such as lead, mercury and cadmium, posing health and environmental risks.

concepts.name: Removal of heavy metal ions by precipitation
concepts.explanation: Treatment strategy where reagents form insoluble compounds with metal ions so they can be removed as precipitates.

concepts.name: Pollution risk of battery heavy metals without recycling
concepts.explanation: Batteries can release heavy metals into the environment if not recycled, increasing potential contamination of water systems.
concepts.broader_concept: Sources and prevention of water pollution

concepts.name: pH meter (principle and use)
concepts.explanation: Instrumental determination of pH using an electrode system that measures potential related to hydrogen ion activity.

concepts.name: Atomic absorption spectroscopy (AAS) for metal analysis
concepts.explanation: Instrumental method that measures absorption of characteristic radiation by ground-state atoms to determine metal ion concentrations (e.g., Pb, Cd) in samples.

concepts.name: Colorimetry for concentration determination
concepts.explanation: Analytical method using light absorption/colour intensity to determine concentration of a coloured species or a coloured product formed in a reaction.

concepts.name: Qualitative tests for anions in water
concepts.explanation: Laboratory tests to identify common anions in aqueous samples using characteristic reactions and observations.

concepts.name: Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD)
concepts.explanation: Measure of the dissolved oxygen required by microorganisms to break down organic matter in water, indicating organic pollution level.

concepts.name: EDTA titration to estimate total water hardness
concepts.explanation: Complexometric titration using EDTA to determine total hardness by measuring Ca2+/Mg2+ concentration; requires balanced ionic equation.

concepts.name: Balanced ionic equation for EDTA complexation (hardness titration)
concepts.explanation: Writing the net ionic reaction representing chelation of metal ions (e.g., Ca2+/Mg2+) by EDTA during hardness titration.

concepts.name: Redox titration to estimate dissolved oxygen
concepts.explanation: Analytical method determining dissolved oxygen content via a redox titration procedure (e.g., iodometric approach), relating titrant volume to oxygen concentration.

concepts.name: Semi-continuous industrial chemical process
concepts.explanation: A hybrid industrial process in which some materials are fed or removed continuously while other steps occur in batches (or periodic intervals).

concepts.name: Feedstock (raw material) selection in industrial processes
concepts.explanation: Choosing suitable raw materials for an industrial chemical process based on availability, cost, purity, and suitability for producing desired products.
concepts.broader_concept: Characteristics of effective industrial chemical processes

concepts.name: Temperature effects on reaction rate
concepts.explanation: How changing temperature alters the speed of a chemical reaction, typically through collision frequency and activation energy considerations.

concepts.name: Pressure effects on reaction rate (gaseous reactions)
concepts.explanation: How changing pressure affects reaction rate for gases by changing concentration and collision frequency.

concepts.name: Catalyst effects on reaction rate
concepts.explanation: How catalysts increase reaction rate by providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy without being consumed overall.

concepts.name: Temperature effects on product yield (industrial optimization)
concepts.explanation: How temperature influences the amount of desired product obtained, often through equilibrium position and side-reaction considerations.

concepts.name: Pressure effects on product yield (industrial optimization)
concepts.explanation: How pressure influences product yield, particularly in reactions involving gases where equilibrium yield depends on total pressure.

concepts.name: Catalyst effects on product yield
concepts.explanation: Understanding that catalysts primarily change how fast equilibrium is reached, and can improve practical yield by reducing side reactions or enabling milder conditions.

concepts.name: Separation of co-products
concepts.explanation: Methods for separating useful by-products from reaction mixtures (e.g., distillation, filtration, chromatography) to enable sale or further processing.
concepts.broader_concept: Product separation and purification in industry

concepts.name: Waste water treatment in chemical industry
concepts.explanation: Processes used to treat aqueous effluent to remove or neutralize contaminants before discharge (e.g., precipitation, neutralization, biological treatment).

concepts.name: Industrial emission control
concepts.explanation: Techniques for reducing harmful gaseous emissions from chemical processes (e.g., scrubbers, catalytic converters, filters) to meet environmental standards.

concepts.name: Industrial chemical process safety
concepts.explanation: Identifying and managing hazards in chemical plants, including training, hazard monitoring, and built-in safety features to prevent accidents.

concepts.name: Heat exchangers for process cost reduction
concepts.explanation: Using heat exchangers to transfer heat between process streams to recover energy and reduce fuel/utility costs in industrial operations.

concepts.name: Recycling unreacted feedstock to reduce costs
concepts.explanation: Returning unreacted reactants to the reactor feed to improve overall conversion and reduce raw material costs.
concepts.broader_concept: Optimizing resource use in industrial processes

concepts.name: Economic impact of waste disposal in chemical processes
concepts.explanation: How disposal and treatment requirements add to variable operating costs and influence process selection and optimization.

concepts.name: Corrosion resistance of chemical plant materials
concepts.explanation: Selection of construction materials for chemical plants based on resistance to corrosion by process chemicals and environmental exposure.
concepts.broader_concept: Materials selection for chemical processing equipment

concepts.name: Chemical inertness (unreactive materials) in plant construction
concepts.explanation: Use of chemically inert materials to prevent unwanted reactions with reactants/products and to maintain process purity and safety.
concepts.broader_concept: Materials selection for chemical processing equipment

concepts.name: Chemistry in water purification
concepts.explanation: Application of chemical processes to provide pure water (e.g., removing contaminants and disinfecting water supplies).

concepts.name: Chemistry in fuel production and use
concepts.explanation: Role of chemistry in producing fuels and understanding their use as energy sources.

concepts.name: Chemistry in metal production
concepts.explanation: Contribution of chemistry to producing and processing metals for societal use.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Chemistry in medicines development
concepts.explanation: Use of chemical knowledge to design, synthesize, and formulate medicines.

concepts.name: Chemistry of detergents
concepts.explanation: Chemical basis for detergent action and the formulation of cleaning agents.

concepts.name: Industrial production and use of enzymes
concepts.explanation: Use of enzymes as chemical/biochemical catalysts in industrial and consumer applications.

concepts.name: Chemistry of dyes and paints
concepts.explanation: Chemical principles behind dyes and paints, including composition and functional performance in coloration and coatings.

concepts.name: Semiconductors as chemical materials
concepts.explanation: Semiconductors as materials whose properties depend on composition and controlled impurities, enabling electronic applications.

concepts.name: Liquid crystals as functional materials
concepts.explanation: Liquid crystals as materials with intermediate order between liquids and solids, used for display and optical applications.

concepts.name: Steam reforming of natural gas for hydrogen production
concepts.explanation: Industrial production of hydrogen from natural gas and water vapour (steam) as a key step in ammonia manufacture.

concepts.name: Water-gas shift reaction
concepts.explanation: Conversion of carbon monoxide and steam to carbon dioxide and hydrogen to increase H2 yield in ammonia feed gas preparation.

concepts.name: Removal of carbon dioxide from synthesis gas
concepts.explanation: Industrial separation step to remove CO2 from hydrogen-rich gas before ammonia synthesis.

concepts.name: Haber process (ammonia synthesis)
concepts.explanation: Formation of ammonia from nitrogen (air) and hydrogen using industrial conditions and a catalyst.

concepts.name: Urea synthesis from ammonia and carbon dioxide
concepts.explanation: Industrial conversion of ammonia (often with CO2) to urea, including recognition that balanced equations are required.

concepts.name: Catalytic oxidation of ammonia to nitrogen monoxide
concepts.explanation: Key Ostwald step where ammonia is oxidised to NO (balanced equation expected).

concepts.name: Oxidation of nitrogen monoxide to nitrogen dioxide
concepts.explanation: Ostwald step converting NO to NO2 (balanced equation expected).

concepts.name: Formation of nitric acid from nitrogen dioxide
concepts.explanation: Reaction step producing HNO3 from NO2 (typically via absorption in water with regeneration of NO).

concepts.name: Formation of ammonium nitrate
concepts.explanation: Industrial synthesis of ammonium nitrate fertiliser from ammonia and nitric acid (neutralisation; balanced equation expected).

concepts.name: Thermal decomposition (calcination) of calcium carbonate to calcium oxide
concepts.explanation: Conversion of CaCO3 to CaO and CO2 as a preparatory step in magnesium oxide manufacture from seawater.
concepts.broader_concept: Preparation of alkaline reagents for precipitation processes

concepts.name: Hydration of calcium oxide to calcium hydroxide (slaking)
concepts.explanation: Reaction of CaO with water to form Ca(OH)2 used to precipitate Mg(OH)2 from seawater-derived Mg2+.
concepts.broader_concept: Preparation of alkaline reagents for precipitation processes

concepts.name: Precipitation of magnesium hydroxide from seawater
concepts.explanation: Formation of Mg(OH)2 by adding calcium hydroxide to seawater containing magnesium ions (balanced equation expected).

concepts.name: Thermal decomposition of magnesium hydroxide to magnesium oxide
concepts.explanation: Conversion of Mg(OH)2 to MgO and water by heating as the final step in MgO manufacture.

concepts.name: Urea as a fertiliser
concepts.explanation: Use of urea as a nitrogen-containing fertiliser in agriculture.
concepts.broader_concept: Applications of industrially produced nitrogen compounds

concepts.name: Ammonium nitrate as a fertiliser
concepts.explanation: Use of ammonium nitrate as a nitrogen fertiliser and its relevance to industrial nitric acid chemistry.
concepts.broader_concept: Applications of industrially produced nitrogen compounds

concepts.name: Magnesium oxide as a refractory material
concepts.explanation: Use of MgO as a heat-resistant (refractory) lining material in furnace walls.

concepts.name: Fractional distillation of liquefied air to produce oxygen
concepts.explanation: Industrial manufacture of oxygen by liquefying air and separating components by fractional distillation based on differing boiling points.

concepts.name: Nitrogen molecule structure and inertness
concepts.explanation: Relationship between N≡N bonding (strong bond) and the low reactivity (inertness) of nitrogen under normal conditions.

concepts.name: Natural fixation of nitrogen
concepts.explanation: Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into biologically usable nitrogen compounds by natural processes (e.g., bacteria, lightning).

concepts.name: Nitrogen and oxygen reactions in an electric discharge
concepts.explanation: Formation of nitrogen oxides when nitrogen and oxygen are subjected to an electric discharge (e.g., lightning conditions).
concepts.broader_concept: Formation of nitrogen oxides in the atmosphere

concepts.name: Combustion of carbon producing carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide
concepts.explanation: How incomplete combustion forms CO while complete combustion forms CO2; represented using balanced chemical equations.

concepts.name: Carbon dioxide dissolved in water: carbonate and hydrogencarbonate species
concepts.explanation: CO2 in water exists as dissolved CO2 and in combined forms as carbonate (CO3^2−) and hydrogencarbonate (HCO3−) ions.

concepts.name: Effect of carbon dioxide on universal indicator (demonstration)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory demonstration showing CO2 dissolving in water to produce an acidic solution, indicated by universal indicator color change.

concepts.name: Greenhouse effect and human influence
concepts.explanation: Warming caused by absorption of infrared radiation by greenhouse gases and how human activities increase atmospheric greenhouse gas levels.

concepts.name: Greenhouse gases and relative effects (CO2, H2O, CH4, CFCs)
concepts.explanation: Identification of major greenhouse gases and comparison of their relative contributions/effects on warming (qualitative emphasis).

concepts.name: Sources of nitrogen oxides and sulfur oxides as air pollutants
concepts.explanation: Natural and anthropogenic sources of NOx and SOx (domestic, industrial, internal combustion engines).

concepts.name: Formation of acids from dissolved nitrogen dioxide and sulfur dioxide
concepts.explanation: Dissolution and reaction of NO2 and SO2 in water to form acidic solutions (key step in acid deposition).

concepts.name: Effect of sulfur dioxide on universal indicator (demonstration)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory demonstration showing SO2 dissolving in water to produce an acidic solution, detected with universal indicator.

concepts.name: Flue gas desulfurization using limestone (scrubbing)
concepts.explanation: Removal of acidic gases (especially SO2) from waste gases by reaction with limestone/calcium carbonate in scrubbers.

concepts.name: Preparation of chloroalkanes by chlorination of alkanes (e.g., methane)
concepts.explanation: Formation of chloroalkanes via substitution reaction of an alkane with chlorine (e.g., chlorination of methane).

concepts.name: Formation of ozone in the stratosphere (equation)
concepts.explanation: Stratospheric ozone formation from oxygen (requires equations, typically involving photodissociation of O2 and recombination to O3).

concepts.name: Photodissociation of ozone (equation)
concepts.explanation: Breakdown of ozone by UV light (requires chemical equation), forming oxygen molecules and/or oxygen atoms.

concepts.name: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs)
concepts.explanation: Identification and basic distinction between CFCs and HCFCs as halogenated organic compounds used in industry and linked to ozone depletion.

concepts.name: Residence time of CFCs in the atmosphere
concepts.explanation: Concept that CFCs persist for long periods in the atmosphere before breakdown, enabling transport to the stratosphere.

concepts.name: Breakdown of CFCs in the stratosphere
concepts.explanation: Photochemical decomposition of CFCs by UV radiation to generate reactive chlorine species.
concepts.broader_concept: Mechanism of ozone depletion by halogens

concepts.name: Catalytic ozone destruction by chlorine atoms (equations)
concepts.explanation: Chain reactions where Cl radicals remove ozone catalytically (equations required), regenerating Cl and converting O3 to O2.
concepts.broader_concept: Mechanism of ozone depletion by halogens

concepts.name: Ozone removal by oxygen atoms and nitrogen monoxide molecules
concepts.explanation: Alternative pathways for ozone depletion involving O atoms and NO molecules (catalytic cycles contributing to ozone loss).

concepts.name: Methane role in absorbing chlorine atoms
concepts.explanation: Methane acting as a sink for reactive chlorine atoms, reducing the concentration of Cl radicals available to destroy ozone.

concepts.name: Replacements for CFCs
concepts.explanation: Alternative chemicals/technologies developed to replace CFCs to reduce ozone depletion impact.

concepts.name: Types of crystalline solids (ionic, molecular, metallic, covalent network)
concepts.explanation: Classification of crystals based on the nature of bonding/forces holding the lattice together: ionic, molecular, metallic and covalent macromolecular (network) crystals.
concepts.broader_concept: Crystal structure and bonding in solids

concepts.name: Relationship between crystal bonding forces and physical properties
concepts.explanation: How the strength and type of binding forces in a crystal (ionic bonds, intermolecular forces, metallic bonding, covalent networks) relate to properties such as hardness, melting point and conductivity.

concepts.name: X-ray crystallography (non-mathematical principle)
concepts.explanation: Determining crystal structure by scattering/diffraction of X-rays by regularly spaced atoms/ions in a crystal to infer lattice arrangement (qualitative treatment).

concepts.name: Addition polymers
concepts.explanation: Polymers formed by addition polymerisation where unsaturated monomers add together without elimination of small molecules, producing long-chain macromolecules.

concepts.name: Monomers
concepts.explanation: Small molecules that can join together repeatedly to form polymers; in addition polymerisation these are typically alkenes.

concepts.name: Poly(ethene) (LDPE vs HDPE)
concepts.explanation: Polymer of ethene; low-density and high-density forms differ due to chain branching and packing, affecting density and mechanical properties.

concepts.name: Structural differences between LDPE and HDPE
concepts.explanation: LDPE has more branching leading to lower crystallinity and density; HDPE is more linear leading to tighter packing, higher crystallinity and density.

concepts.name: Poly(chloroethene) (PVC)
concepts.explanation: Addition polymer formed from chloroethene (vinyl chloride) monomers; properties influenced by polar C–Cl bonds and chain interactions.

concepts.name: Poly(phenylethene) (polystyrene)
concepts.explanation: Addition polymer formed from phenylethene (styrene); aromatic side groups affect rigidity and brittleness depending on structure.

concepts.name: Poly(tetrafluoroethene) (PTFE)
concepts.explanation: Addition polymer formed from tetrafluoroethene; strong C–F bonds and low intermolecular attractions contribute to chemical resistance and low friction.

concepts.name: Poly(propene) (polypropylene)
concepts.explanation: Addition polymer formed from propene; methyl side groups influence crystallinity and physical properties such as stiffness and melting point.

concepts.name: Physical properties of polymers: density, flexibility, hardness
concepts.explanation: Key measurable properties used to compare polymers and link polymer structure (chain packing, branching, side groups) to material performance.

concepts.name: Recycling process for plastics (sorting to re-extrusion)
concepts.explanation: Typical mechanical recycling stages: sorting, shredding, washing, drying and re-extrusion to produce reusable plastic feedstock.

concepts.name: Recycling of polystyrene (as an example)
concepts.explanation: Application of the mechanical recycling stages specifically to polystyrene, highlighting practical handling and processing considerations.

concepts.name: Comparison of metals and non-metals (physical properties)
concepts.explanation: Typical differences in hardness, lustre, malleability, ductility, and thermal/electrical conductivity between metals and non-metals.

concepts.name: Alloys
concepts.explanation: Mixtures of metals (or a metal with small amounts of other elements) designed to modify properties such as strength, hardness and corrosion resistance.

concepts.name: Effect of carbon content in steel on hardness
concepts.explanation: How varying carbon in iron (steel) changes hardness/strength by influencing the metal lattice and resistance to deformation.

concepts.name: Voltage in a simple cell depends on metal combination
concepts.explanation: Different pairs of metals in a simple cell produce different potential differences because their tendencies to be oxidized/reduced differ.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolysis of molten lead(II) bromide (inert electrodes)
concepts.explanation: Decomposition of molten PbBr2 by electric current using inert electrodes to produce lead at the cathode and bromine at the anode.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Writing half-equations for electrolysis
concepts.explanation: Representing oxidation at the anode and reduction at the cathode using balanced ionic half-equations for an electrolytic process.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Relative corrodability of metals
concepts.explanation: Comparing how readily different metals corrode based on their reactivity/oxidation tendencies and environmental conditions.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Corrosion prevention by galvanising
concepts.explanation: Protecting iron/steel by coating with zinc, which acts as a barrier and also provides sacrificial protection if scratched.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Corrosion prevention by surface coating
concepts.explanation: Reducing corrosion by applying a physical barrier (e.g., paint or polymer coating) that limits contact with oxygen and water.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Protective oxide layers on aluminium and chromium
concepts.explanation: Al and Cr form adherent oxide films that hinder further oxidation, providing corrosion resistance (passivation).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Sacrificial anode protection
concepts.explanation: Corrosion control method where a more reactive metal is attached so it oxidizes preferentially, protecting the main metal.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Extraction of sodium in the Downs cell
concepts.explanation: Industrial electrolysis of molten sodium chloride (often with additives) to produce sodium metal at the cathode and chlorine at the anode.
concepts.broader_concept: Industrial extraction of highly electropositive metals
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Processing bauxite to pure alumina
concepts.explanation: Converting bauxite ore into purified aluminium oxide (alumina) as a prerequisite for aluminium extraction by electrolysis.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolytic extraction of aluminium from alumina
concepts.explanation: Producing aluminium by electrolysis of alumina (in molten electrolyte) where Al3+ is reduced to Al at the cathode and oxide ions are oxidized at the anode.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Chlorine as a by-product of electrolysis in metal extraction
concepts.explanation: Formation of chlorine gas at the anode during electrolysis of chloride-containing melts/brines, making chlorine an industrial by-product.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Anodising of aluminium
concepts.explanation: An electrolytic process that thickens the aluminium oxide layer on aluminium to improve corrosion resistance and surface properties.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Porous oxide layer from anodising enables dyeing
concepts.explanation: The anodised aluminium oxide layer is porous, allowing dyes to enter and be sealed, producing durable coloration.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Environmental aspects of aluminium production
concepts.explanation: Environmental impacts associated with aluminium extraction and processing, including energy use and emissions/waste considerations.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Role of cheap electricity in aluminium extraction economics
concepts.explanation: Aluminium electrolysis is energy-intensive, so electricity cost strongly influences the feasibility and location of aluminium production.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Transition elements: variable valency
concepts.explanation: Transition (d-block) elements commonly exhibit more than one stable oxidation state due to involvement of both ns and (n−1)d electrons in bonding.
concepts.broader_concept: General chemical properties of transition elements

concepts.name: Transition metal compounds: colour
concepts.explanation: Many transition metal ions/compounds are coloured, typically due to electronic transitions involving d-orbitals in partially filled d-subshells.
concepts.broader_concept: General chemical properties of transition elements

concepts.name: Transition elements as catalysts
concepts.explanation: Transition metals and their compounds are widely used as catalysts because they can provide alternative reaction pathways and often change oxidation state during catalysis.

concepts.name: Blast furnace: chemical aspects of iron manufacture
concepts.explanation: Iron extraction in a blast furnace involves reduction of iron oxides by carbon monoxide (from coke), formation of slag using limestone, and separation of molten iron.

concepts.name: Electric arc process for steel manufacture (main stages)
concepts.explanation: Electric arc steelmaking uses an electric arc to melt scrap/charge, followed by refining steps to adjust composition and remove impurities (outline level).

concepts.name: Environmental impacts of iron and steel production
concepts.explanation: Iron and steelmaking can cause environmental issues such as CO2 emissions, air pollutants (dust/particulates), and waste slag; understanding these impacts is part of industrial chemistry context.

concepts.name: Systematic (IUPAC) versus traditional names in organic chemistry
concepts.explanation: Organic compounds may have both systematic (IUPAC) names and traditional/common names; curricula may require systematic naming while recognising common-name usage.

concepts.name: Traditional names not examinable when paired with systematic names
concepts.explanation: When a traditional name is provided alongside a systematic name, the traditional name may be for recognition only and not required for assessment.
